voyage.name: Black Sesame Kitchen
voyage.address: 3 Black Sesame Hutong, Dongcheng District
voyage.content: Try your hand at creating a variety of Chinese dishes, from cold starters to famous noodles and dumplings. Classes are conducted in English, and you can also enjoy a fancy dinner with explanations of major flavors and the significance of different ingredients. Reservations are required.

voyage.name: Beijing Cookery
voyage.content: Join a cooking class focused on Hutong cuisine, offering hands-on experiences in preparing traditional dishes. An optional market tour is available for an additional fee.

voyage.name: The Hutong
voyage.address: 1 Jiu Dao Wan Zhong Xiang Hutong, Dongcheng District (东城区九道湾中巷1号)
voyage.content: Located in a traditional courtyard home in downtown Beijing, The Hutong offers a variety of Chinese cultural programs. Visitors can attend market tours, cooking classes (both Chinese and international), tea tastings, and traditional Chinese medicine sessions. You can also enjoy private meals, events, or simply relax on the rooftop terrace with a view of authentic hutong culture. Chefs, guides, and teachers speak Engl

voyage.name: Beihai Park
voyage.content: Beihai is a former imperial garden centred on a lake with interesting religious and garden architecture. There's a big island and white pagoda which was built in the 17th century. The giant buildings westward outside are PRC's Ministry of Defence and General Staff, which, to be honest, ruin the scene of the west bank. On the north bank, you can visit some small but beautiful gardens. Beihai is a good place to take a

voyage.name: Beijing Zoo and Aquarium
voyage.alt: 北京动物园 Běijīng Dòngwù Yuán
voyage.hours: Zoo: Apr-Oct 07:30-18:00; Zoo Nov-Mar 07:30-17:00; Aquarium Apr-Oct 09:00-17:30; Aquarium Nov-Mar 09:00-17:00
voyage.content: (They do have pandas but displays aren't as good as other places in China, such as the Panda Breeding Centre in Chengdu, Sichuan Province). The animals are kept in very small cages in which they pace to and fro in sheer restlessness and desperation. The lion and tiger building is particularly disappointing, housing a collection of large felines in concrete cages without any natural habitation. The pandas are relative

voyage.name: Jingshan Park
voyage.address: Jingshan Front Street
voyage.content: Jingshan is another former imperial garden with some imperial garden architecture. A popular next stop after leaving the Forbidden City from the north gate, this 23-hectare (57-acre) park is built around Jingshan, the artificial hill created with the soil dug to build the Forbidden City's moat. Literally meaning "Prospect Hill", it is also variously known as Coal Hill or Feng Shui Hill. Those who make the climb from

voyage.name: Grand View Garden
voyage.address: South Caiyuan Street (南菜园街12号 Náncàiyuánjiē)
voyage.content: Garden established in the 1980s based on the novel 'The Dream of the Red Mansions'. 125,000 m² with temples, pavilions and other buildings as well as miniature gardens. Traditional ceremonies performed now and then. The park also has a restaurant.

voyage.name: Taoranting Park
voyage.address: 19 Taiping Jie (太平街19号 Tàipíngjiē)
voyage.content: A former hangout for literati, while most other Beijing parks were for imperial families only. The park has a total area of 240,000 m² with water area accounting for 69,000 m². The park is a mixture of ancient construction styles and modern park design. It was built in 1952. Taoran Pavilion (one of the four most important in Beijing) build in 1695 and some tombs are located in the park. The park has a lake with pavil

voyage.name: Xibianmen City Wall Relics Park
voyage.content: The section of Ming-era city wall in this area was constructed in the fourth year of the Zhengtong reign (1439) and formed part of Beijing's Inner City wall. The central portion retains the junction where it connected with the Outer City wall, while the southern section consists of the surviving rampart base of the Inner City's Southwest Corner Tower. To the west of this segment of the Inner City wall once stood Xibi

voyage.name: Temple of the Moon Park
voyage.content: The altar was built in 1530 during the Ming Dynasty for use in ritual sacrifice to the Moon by the Emperor of China. The altar and the surrounding grounds are within a public park. The altar is no longer intact, though the surrounding walls remain.

voyage.name: Miaoying Temple
voyage.alt: 妙应寺 Miàoyìng Sì; 白塔寺 Báitǎ Sì
voyage.content: Nepalese-style white pagoda older and larger than the white pagoda in the Beihai Park.

voyage.name: White Cloud Temple
voyage.address: 6 Baiyunguan Street (白云观街6号 Báiyúnguànjiē)
voyage.content: Taoist temple established in 793. Houses the Chinese Taoist Association and a Taoist Health Clinic.

voyage.name: Guanghua Temple
voyage.address: 31 Ya'er Hutong (后海鸦儿胡同31号 Hòuhǎiyāérhútòng)
voyage.content: Buddhist temple used to pray for success in business life.

voyage.name: Guangji Temple
voyage.alt: 广济寺 Guǎngjìsì; also known as Temple of Great Charity
voyage.hours: 08:00-15:50 but only partly open to the public
voyage.address: Fuchengmennei Street (阜成门内大街 Fùchéngménnèidàjiē)
voyage.content: Buddhist temple built around 1460. Burned down in 1934 and was rebuilt in 1952 and further renovated in 1972. It is supposed to look as it used to, but it does not really look old. The temple is functioning as a center for Buddhist thinking and learning and it is also the headquarters of the Chinese Buddhist Association.

voyage.name: Lidai Diwang Miao
voyage.alt: 历代帝王庙 Lìdàidìwángmiào; also known as Temple to Emperors of Past Ages
voyage.address: 131 Fuchengmennei Street (阜成门内大街131号 Fùchéngménnèidàjiē)
voyage.content: Large temple built in 1530 used to sacrifice to past emperors. Opened to the public in 2004 after a decade of renovation. Here can be seen memorial tablets for many past emperors.

voyage.name: Fayuan Monastery
voyage.address: Fayuansihou Street (法源寺后街 Fǎyuánsìhòujiē)
voyage.content: This Buddhist temple was built in 645 and rebuilt in 1436-1449, which makes it the oldest existing in Beijing. Now, it is the site of the Chinese Buddhist Academy and the exhibition center for Buddhist cultural relics, and is also an important institution training young monks and Buddhism research. The temple covers 6,700 square meters. The main buildings are Gate of Temple, Heavenly King Hall, Main Hall, Hall of Gre

voyage.name: Baoguo Temple
voyage.address: Baoguosi Qianjie, Guang'anmennei Dajie (广安门内大街报国寺前街 Guǎngānménnèidàjiēbàoguósìqiánjiē)
voyage.content: Founded in 1103, various uses during the next centuries, almost forgotten after 1949, but now renovated and open to public. There is also an antique market specialized in picture books and calligraphies, including writing tools and paper.

voyage.name: Temple of Agriculture
voyage.content: See the Museum of Ancient Architecture.

voyage.name: Changchun Temple
voyage.content: Built by the Wanli Emperor's mother in 1592 during the Ming dynasty, it's also the Xuannan Cultural Museum.

voyage.name: Huode Zhenjun Temple
voyage.content: A Taoist temple built during the Ming Dynasty and then rebuilt in 1759 during the Qing Dynasty.

voyage.name: Tianning Temple
voyage.alt: 天宁寺, 天寧寺(Tiānníng Sì)
voyage.content: A Liao Dynasty Buddhist temple. It functions as a nunnery. Within its grounds stands Beijing's tallest dense-eave brick pagoda.

voyage.name: Beijing City God Temple
voyage.content: It was established in the Yuan Dynasty (1270), reconstructed during the Ming Dynasty. In the tenth year of the Tongzhi era of the Qing Dynasty (1871), the temple was destroyed by fire. Only five buildings remain standing.

voyage.name: Capital Museum
voyage.price: Free, tickets must be reserved three days in advance on the official website
voyage.address: 16 Fuxingmenwai St (复兴门外大街16号 Fùxīngménwài Dàjiē)
voyage.content: New high profile history and art museum located in an impressive building. Exhibits include the history of Beijing and artifacts from throughout China's history.

voyage.name: Prince Gong's Mansion and Garden
voyage.address: 14A Liuyin St (柳荫街14号 Liǔyìnjiē
voyage.content: The mansion displays the life of princes during the Qing dynasty. The garden is packed with Chinese tourists. The mansion stages Peking Opera and magic shows now and then.

voyage.name: Soong Ching Ling's Former Residence
voyage.address: 46 Houhai North Riverside (后海北沿46号 Hòuhǎiběiyàn)
voyage.content: Museum and garden showing the life of Soong Ching Ling (1893-1981). Soong was a politician in the early days of communist China, vice president 1959–1975. She was married to Sun Yat-sen and also related to Chiang Kai-shek.

voyage.name: Mei Lanfang's Residence
voyage.alt: 梅兰芳纪念馆 Méilánfāng Jìniànguǎn
voyage.address: 9 Huguosi Rd (护国寺路9号 Hùguósìlù)
voyage.content: Museum showing the life of Mei Lanfang (1894-1961). Mei was the greatest star of Peking Opera, acting for more than 50 years, primarily playing female roles. Furniture as well as costumes and other opera stuff are exhibited here.

voyage.name: Guo Moruo's Former Residence
voyage.alt: 郭沫若故居 Guō Mòruò gùjū
voyage.address: 18 Qianhai W St (前海西街18号 Qiánhǎi Xījiē)
voyage.content: Museum showing the life of Guo Moruo (1892-1978). Guo was an author, poet, historian and government official. His works seems quite dated now, but his former residence is still worth a visit.

voyage.name: Beijing Science Center
voyage.address: 1 North Third Ring Road Middle Rd (三北环中路1号 Sānběihuánzhōnglù)
voyage.content: Educational museum with the possibility of experimenting yourself. See also: the new location (the main branch) - Hall A has short films, Hall B has exhibitions, whereas Hall C is an experimental area primarily for children.

voyage.name: Xu Beihong Museum
voyage.alt: 徐悲鸿纪念馆 Xúbēihóng Jìniànguǎn
voyage.address: 53 Xinjiekou Beidajie (新街口北大街53号 Xīnjiēkǒuběidàjiē)
voyage.content: Xu Beihong (1895-1953) was one of the first and most influential modern Chinese painters. He used both Chinese and Western techniques and is most famous for traditional painting of running horses. The museum exhibits a large number of his own works as well as his large collection of other artists' works.

voyage.name: Beijing Lu Xun Museum
voyage.alt: 北京鲁迅博物馆 Běijīng Lǔxùn Bówùguǎn
voyage.address: 19 Gongmenkou Ertiao, Fuchengmennei (阜成门内宫门口二条19号 Fùchèngménnèi Gōngménkǒuèrtiáo)
voyage.content: Lu Xun (1881-1936) was one of the first and most influential modern Chinese writers. He is most famous for "The True Story of Ah Q". The museum consist of Lu Xun's former residence as well as an exhibition hall with exhibits of Lu Xun's personal effects, originals and copies of his works and also exhibits not dirictly related to Lu Xun.

voyage.name: Beijing Ancient Architecture Museum
voyage.alt: 北京古代建筑博物馆 Gǔdàijiànzhùbówùguǎn
voyage.hours: 09:00-17:00, closed on Mondays except public holidays
voyage.address: 21 Dongjing Road (东经路21号; Dōngjīnglù)
voyage.content: Part of the Temple of Agriculture, museum with a model of Beijing ancient city as well as exhibits of Beijing's ancient architecture, famous for two caissons moved from the Longfu Temple(隆福寺). Free volunteer guide time: 09:30-11:00 and 14:00-15:30 during weekdays, 09:30-11:00, 10:30-12:00, 14:00-15:30, 15:00-16:30 during weekends and holidays. The waiting area of volunteer guide is at the entrance of Shenchu(神厨) yard

voyage.name: Museum of Ancient Pottery Civilization
voyage.alt: 古陶文明博物馆 Gǔtáo Wénmíng Bówùguǎn
voyage.address: 12 South Caiyuan West Street (南菜园西街12号 Náncàiyuán Xījiē)
voyage.content: Shows the Chinese history of pottery from Neolithic Age to now.

voyage.name: Paleozoological Museum of China
voyage.hours: 09:00-16:30, no tickets sold after 16:00, closed on Mondays
voyage.address: 142 Xizhimenwai Street (西直门外大街142号)

voyage.name: Former residence of Shen Jiaben
voyage.content: was a Chinese jurist and politician in modern times. He presided over the legislation in the late Qing Dynasty and was the founder and pioneer of modern Chinese jurisprudence.

voyage.name: Deshengmen
voyage.address: North Ring Rd Two (北二环路 Běièrhuánlù)
voyage.content: City gate built in 1437 as part of the city wall, which was torn down in 1969. Now only an archery tower and a barbican is left. The gate houses an ancient coin exhibition and a snack bar.

voyage.name: Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception
voyage.content: Established by Jesuit missionaries in 1605, it is the oldest Roman Catholic church in Beijing. Sunday masses in Chinese are held early in the morning (06:00, 07:00, and 08:30), offering the experience to hear the local faithful chanting Christian prayers in Chinese, as they have been for centuries. English masses (10:30 and 15:00) and an Italian mass (12:30) are popular with foreigners.

voyage.name: Niujie (Niu Street) Mosque
voyage.address: 88 Niu Street (牛街88号 Niújiē)
voyage.content: Famous Mosque build in 996 and the oldest and largest of the mosques in Beijing. Structured as a traditional Chinese palace, but also uses typical Arabic decoration with a lot of red colour. A must see if staying for more than a few days. The Muslim presence in the area is obvious with many Muslim shops and Arabic signs around.

voyage.name: Great Hall of the People
voyage.content: Seat of China's parliament and venue for important political meetings. While the hall is normally used for meetings for the National People's Congress, there are occasionally classical-music concerts held there.

voyage.name: Zhongnanhai
voyage.address: 174 West Chang'an Avenue
voyage.content: This former imperial garden centered on two lakes is now the headquarters of China's government and ruling party. The compound is not to the public, but you can take a photo in front of the distinctive south gate and revolutionary slogans fronting West Chang'an Avenue. You can also see the back of the compound from the south side of Beihai Park, from which it is separated by a bridge.

voyage.name: Church of the Saviour
voyage.alt: 西什库天主堂; 北堂
voyage.content: A historic Catholic church established by the French Jesuits and completed in 1703.

voyage.name: Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception
voyage.alt: 圣母无染原罪堂, 宣武门天主堂, 南堂
voyage.content: The original foundation of the cathedral was in 1605, making it the oldest Catholic church in Beijing, the current building in Baroque style dates from 1904.

voyage.name: National Assembly Building
voyage.content: The first purpose-built meeting place of the National Assembly of the Republic of China in Beijing. It is now part of the compound of Xinhua News Agency.

voyage.name: Huguang Huiguan Theatre
voyage.address: 3 Hufang Street (虎坊路3号 Hǔfānglù)
voyage.content: Theatre primarily performing excerpts of traditional Chinese opera. The theatre has been working since the 1830s. The theatre building from 1830 is the oldest and best preserved indoor theatre in Beijing. It is in area with other traditional buildings. Next to the theatre is an opera museum.

voyage.name: Lao She Teahouse
voyage.content: See listing in Drink section.

voyage.name: Li Yuan Theatre
voyage.address: 175 Yong'anlu (永安路175号 Yǒng'ānlù)
voyage.content: Plays from the Beijing Opera repertoire. Also exhibitions of opera costumes and other. Tea and snacks available.

voyage.name: Tianqiao Theatre
voyage.address: Beiwei Road (北纬路30号 Běiwěilù)
voyage.content: Theater with a seating capacity of 1,200 with performance of local folk music and dance, talk shows, and international ballet and musicals.

voyage.name: Tsinghua Chi
voyage.content: A spa experience from the famous Qinghua Chi, established in 1905. Great service. Affordable TCM treatments. Try the Ba Guan (Cupping) or acupuncture or opt for simpler manicure and pedicure and Massage.

voyage.name: Beijing Exhibition Center
voyage.address: 135 Xizhimenwai St (西直门外大街135号 Xīzhíménwàidàjiē)
voyage.content: The 1,000-seat Beijing Exhibition Theater (北京展览馆剧场 Běijīng Zhǎnlǎnguǎn Jùchǎng) is one of the main elements of the Beijing Exhibition Center, a multi-functional building including an exhibition hall, hotel, restaurants and entertainment. The theater hosts a wide range of shows including Chinese plays, Western and Chinese operas and ballets, musicals and rock concerts. Built in 1954 during the height of Sino-Soviet co

voyage.name: Ethnic Cultural Palace Theatre
voyage.alt: 民族文化宫大剧院 Mínzúwénhuàgōng Dàjùyuàn
voyage.address: 49 Fuxingmennei St (复兴门内大街49号 Fùxīngménnèidàjiē)
voyage.content: Performances of classical music, ballet, musical, opera, drama plays and movies.

voyage.name: People's Theater
voyage.address: 74 Huguosi St (护国寺大街74号 Hùguósì Dàjiē)

voyage.name: PLA Song and Dance Theater
voyage.alt: 解放军歌舞剧院 Jiěfàng Jūngēwǔ Jùyuàn
voyage.address: 60 Deshengmennei St (德胜门内大街60号 Déshèngménnèi Dàjiē)

voyage.name: Beijing Concert Hall
voyage.address: 1 Beixinhua St (北新华街1号 Běixīnhuá Jiē)

voyage.name: Central Conservatory of Music
voyage.alt: 中央音乐学院 Zhōngyāng Yīnyuè Xuéyuàn
voyage.address: 43 Baojia St (鲍家街43号 Bàojiā Jiē)
voyage.content: The main purpose of the conservatory is to educate musicians. Concerts now and then.

voyage.name: Forbidden City Concert Hall
voyage.content: Various events are held here.

voyage.name: National Centre for the Performing Arts
voyage.address: 2 West Chang'an St (西长安街2号 Xīcháng'ān Jiē)
voyage.content: Theater complex with three halls (opera, music and theater) covering almost 12,000 m² and seating a total of 5,452 people. One of the most stunning buildings in Beijing and a must see even if not attending an opera or concert.

voyage.name: Lakes of Shichahai
voyage.content: A large area north of Beihai Park that encompasses 3 adjacent lakes (Xihai, Houhai, and Qianhai) enjoyed by locals for a long stroll along the lakes. The quiet lake area turns into a busy nightlife hub around the crossing point of the eastern end of Houhai and Qianhai.

voyage.name: Beijing Planetarium
voyage.alt: 北京天文馆新馆 Běijīng Tiānwén Guǎnxīnguǎn
voyage.address: 138 Xizhimenwai St (西直门外大街138号 Xīzhíménwàidàjiē)
voyage.content: Here you can watch movement of stars and planets, creation of the solar system, evolution of life, space shuttle simulation and the history of the sun.

voyage.name: Philippe Active Space Station
voyage.alt: 菲利普宇宙空间站 Fēilìpǔ Yǔzhòu Kōngjiān Zhàn
voyage.address: 43 Pinganli Xidajie (平安里西大街43号 Píngānlǐ Xīdàjiē)
voyage.content: Play center for children including ball pool, maze and arts and crafts area.

voyage.name: Beijing Capital Times Square
voyage.alt: 首都时代广场 Shǒu​dū​ Shí​dài​ Guǎng​chǎng​
voyage.address: 88 Xi Chang'an St (西长安街88号 Xī​cháng​'ān​jiē​)
voyage.content: Shopping center focusing on international brands.

voyage.name: Grand Pacific
voyage.address: 133 Xidan North St (西单北大街133号 Xī​dān​běi​dà​jiē​)
voyage.content: Has a good selection of less expensive brands and attracts primarily younger shoppers. The shopping mall appears bright and clean and it is usually not too crowded. Here you can find makeup, clothes and sports. Restaurants include Bread Talk, DQ, Pizza Hut and Sizzler.

voyage.name: Joy City
voyage.address: 130 Xidan North St (西单北大街130号 Xī​dān​běi​dà​jiē)
voyage.content: This mall opened in 2008 is the largest in Xidan and you can find almost everything here including an enormous cosmetic shop. The building has an impressive glass facade, and inside the feel is spacious despite the hordes of locals browsing here.

voyage.name: Xidan Department Store
voyage.address: 120 Xidan North St (西单北大街120号 Xī​dān​běi​dà​jiē​)
voyage.content: Government owned mall with a history of more than 70 years. It has been redecorated several times over the years but still appears a bit old fashioned. The prices are good though.

voyage.name: Hanguang Department Store
voyage.address: 176 Xidan North St
voyage.content: Formerly Zhong You Department Store (中友百货). Has a lot of fake brands (mostly clothes). Very affordable if you bargain hard. There is a Sanrio gift shop on the fifth floor.

voyage.name: Qianmen Dajie Pedestrian Street
voyage.content: One of Beijing's oldest commercial streets with a 500 year old history, situated south of Qianmen, the old southern gate of the city. Now, this street has been reconstructed to bring it back as it was in the 1920s. Furthermore, there are trolley cars (¥50 for a ticket) that have re-appeared on the street, after being absent for 40 years. The street is a popular destination for tourists as of 2021. Many of the famous

voyage.name: Dashilan
voyage.content: Dashilan (and surrounding streets) is a shopping area dating back to the Ming dynasty. The name means big fences, which in earlier times were in place in both ends of the street. Everything burned down during the Boxer Rebellion in 1900, but the area has since been reestablished as a shopping area.

voyage.name: Daoxiangcun
voyage.address: Zhubaoshi Street (珠宝市街 Zhūbǎoshìjiē)
voyage.content: Famous shop established in 1895. Best known for its wide selection of southern style cakes. More than 20 branches around the city.

voyage.name: Liubiju
voyage.address: Zhubaoshi Street (珠宝市街 Zhūbǎoshìjiē)
voyage.content: Famous shop established in 1530. Sells pickled vegetables.

voyage.name: Liulichang
voyage.content: There is no production here any more, but rather antique stores, selling Chinese painting, handicrafts, and used books. The area was popular back to the Tang dynasty, but the small shops were amalgamated into state-operated units during the 1950s. It was redeveloped as a tourist area after 1979, but has failed to regain its former popularity. Nevertheless, it is picturesque and you can still find interesting things h

voyage.name: Beijing Qianxiangyi Silk Store
voyage.alt: 北京谦祥益丝绸商店 Běijīng Qiānxiángyì Sīchóu Shāngdiàn
voyage.address: 50 Dazhalan West Street (大栅栏西街50号 Dàzhàlánxījiē)
voyage.content: Very large silk store established in 1840. Claims to be the biggest silk professional store in China.

voyage.name: Tea Street
voyage.address: Maliandao Chayecheng (马连道茶叶城 Mǎliándàocháyèchéng)
voyage.content: The street has 8 wholesale tea markets and more than 600 tea shops. Tea sets also for sale here.

voyage.name: Sogo
voyage.address: 8 Xuanwumenwai Street (宣武门外大街8号 Xuānwǔménwàidàjiē)
voyage.content: Shopping mall with Japanese and European shops.

voyage.name: Carrefour
voyage.address: 11 Malian Dao (马连道11号 Mǎliándào)
voyage.content: French supermarket.

voyage.name: Xizhimen
voyage.content: One of the most popular markets for locals is located in Xizhimen, next to the zoo. To get there, in front of the zoo there is a new huge building, which is just another big market, but behind it, there is the wholesale market, with the best prices, and a lot of genuine goods (clothing). This market is much more local than others listed here, and is perhaps not ideal for the less adventurous traveler. There is also a

voyage.name: Sihuan Mixed Goods Market
voyage.alt: 四环综合市场 Sìhuán Zōnghé Shìchǎng
voyage.address: Sihuan Hutong, Deshengmenne St (德胜门内大街四环胡同 Déshèngménnèi Dàjiē Sìhuán Hútòng)
voyage.content: Raw food whole sale market.

voyage.name: Beijing Commodity Market
voyage.address: 259 Fuwai Rd
voyage.content: 40,000-m² market offering a wide range of products including fashion, gifts, leather goods and toys.

voyage.name: Tian Zhao Tian Market
voyage.content: Jewelry market.

voyage.name: Jiumen Xiaochi
voyage.address: 1 Xiaoyou Hutong (孝友胡同1号 Xiàoyǒuhútòng)
voyage.content: This traditional place hidden in the hutongs close to Houhai houses ten or so vendors. Before choosing from the many different simple and traditional dishes here, you will have to go to the cashier and add value to the shared charge card. This is a very popular place with locals and can be packed, especially in weekends around lunch and dinner time. A great place to get a feel of old Beijing.

voyage.name: Ri Chang
voyage.address: 14 Di'anmen W Ave (地安门西大街14号 Dìānménxī Dàjiē)
voyage.content: Simple Cantonese restaurant with good food but unimpressive service and decoration.

voyage.name: Nevertheless Café
voyage.address: No.37 Beiguanfang Hutong 西城区北官房胡同37号
voyage.content: A cool bar by the side of Houhai Lake.

voyage.name: Lanhuahua Restaurant
voyage.alt: 兰花花美食村 Lánhuā Huāměi Shícūn
voyage.address: Tianqiao Hotel, No.11, Xijing Lu
voyage.content: Serves Shaanxi cuisine.

voyage.name: Fengyuan Baozipu
voyage.address: Xinjiekou Inner St (西城区新街口外大街 Xīn​jiē​kǒu​wài​dà​jiē​)
voyage.content: Cantonese cuisine. Serves simple dishes like baozi, congee, doufu soup. Very busy at lunch.

voyage.name: Shaguoju
voyage.address: Xisi South St (西四南大街60号 Xīsìnán​ St)
voyage.content: Manchurian cuisine. This restaurant has been around for centuries, but surprisingly the service is still good and the prices low despite the increasing popularity. Specialties include Boiled Pork Casserole (砂锅白肉 shā​guō​bái​ròu​), which is said to have been served for Emperor Qing in the 18th century. Also the Nine Pig Guts (九转肥肠 jiǔ​zhuàn​féi​cháng) is worth a try.

voyage.name: Koufuju
voyage.address: 93 Taipingqiao St (太平桥大街93号 Tài​píng​qiáo​ Dà​jiē​)
voyage.content: Restaurant specialising in hot pot with a large selection of meat to choose from.

voyage.name: Charme
voyage.address: 1 Dayue Building 6, 131 Xidan North St (西单北大街131号大悦城6楼01号 Xī​dān​běi​ Dà​jiē​, Dàyuè​chéng​lóu​)
voyage.content: Cantonese restaurant popular with Hong Kong expats and tourists.

voyage.name: Qingzhen Xiaochi
voyage.address: 68 Mianhua Hutong (棉花胡同68号 Miánhua Hútòng)
voyage.content: Simple and cheap Beijing cuisine, eg fried noodles. Busy serving elderly locals who appears to come here almost every day.

voyage.name: Xi'an Restaurant
voyage.address: 20 Xinjiekou South St (新街口南大街20号 Xīnjiēkǒu Nán​dà​jiē​)
voyage.content: Xi'an cuisine. Serves halal dishes. This restaurant has a long history, and is said to have been a favorite of Chairman Mao. Specialties include mutton soup and steamed mutton.

voyage.name: Xidan Chiku
voyage.address: 15 Zhongsheng Hutong (钟声胡同15号 Zhōngshēng Hútòng)
voyage.content: Serves Beijing cuisine specialising in chicken wings.

voyage.name: Ma Bashi Restaurant
voyage.address: 37 Xubjiekou East St (新街口东街37号 Xīnjiēkǒu Dōngjiē)
voyage.content: Busy small restaurant specialising in beef noodles and Xinjiang noodles.

voyage.name: Jinfuyuan
voyage.alt: 金福源桂林米粉 Jīn​fú​yuán​ Guì​lín​mǐ​fěn​
voyage.address: 72 Xinjiekou Dongjie (新街口东街72号 Xīnjiēkǒu dōngdà​jiē​)
voyage.content: Small restaurant popular with locals. Serves Beijing cuisine, specialising in rice casserole and rice noodles.

voyage.name: Kong Yi Ji
voyage.address: South bank of Houhai (后海南岸 Hòuǎi Nánàn)
voyage.content: Traditional Zhejiang cuisine in modern surroundings.

voyage.name: Cafe Sambal
voyage.address: 43 Doufuchi Hutong, Gulou Ave
voyage.content: Traditional authentic Malaysian cuisine and flavours.

voyage.name: Sichuan Restaurant
voyage.address: B14 Liuyin St (柳荫街14号 Liǔ​yìn​jiē​)
voyage.content: Sichuan cuisine.

voyage.name: Hutong Pizza
voyage.address: 9 Yindingqiao Hutong (银锭桥胡同9号 Yín​dìng​qiáo ​Hú​tòng​)
voyage.content: Small courtyard restaurant serving both typical and more sophisticated pizzas. Quite limited selection of beers.

voyage.name: Kao Rou Ji
voyage.address: 14 Qianhai Dongyan (前海东沿14号 Qián​hǎi​dōng​yàn​)
voyage.content: Halal restaurant specialising in Beijing-style roast lamb/mutton and beef, but best known for the lamb/mutton. This restaurant has been around for more than 100 years and has great views of the lake from the second floor. A favourite of the Prince Regent Zaifeng in the 19th century. In the early 20th century it was one of three famed roast meat restaurants in Beijing.

voyage.name: Yu Hua Tai
voyage.address: 23 Yuzhongxili Residence, Yumin Road
voyage.content: Since 1921, diners have been coming to the time-honored restaurant to enjoy its authentic, no-frills Huaiyang cooking made by chefs who cooked for the first banquent on the founding night of China in 1949, with dishes like scorched eel with garlic and soy, stir-fried prawns with vegetables, fried yellow fish with chopped vegetables, and Huangqiao sesame cake.

voyage.name: Little Sheep
voyage.address: 43 Guang'anmennei Dajie (光安门内大街43号 Guāng'ānménnèi Dàjiē)
voyage.content: Mongolian hot pot restaurant with branches nationwide and abroad. Richer soup and, therefore, no dipping sauce.

voyage.name: Tan Yu Tou
voyage.address: 25 Zhushikou West Street (珠市口西大街临25号 Zhūshìkǒu Xīdàjiēlín)
voyage.content: Primarily serves spicy Sichuan hotpot with fish or meat.

voyage.name: Yuxin Sichuan Restaurant
voyage.address: Xidan Saite Building, 7F (西单塞特7层 Xīdān Sàitè Qīcéng)
voyage.content: One of the contenders in the ongoing competition for Beijing's best Szechuan cooking, Yuxin delivers on authenticity, flavor, and service. It's always busy, and always good.

voyage.name: Kao Rou Wan
voyage.address: 58 Nanlishi Rd (南礼士路58号)
voyage.content: Xinjiang cuisine specialising in roast meats.

voyage.name: Xiang E Qing
voyage.address: 3 Jiaoyu St (教育街3号)
voyage.content: Hunan and Hubei cuisine.

voyage.name: Beijing Ren Grand Restaurant
voyage.address: 6 Erqi Juchang Rd (二七剧场路甲6号)
voyage.content: Cantonese cuisine.

voyage.name: Hui Feng Hot Pot
voyage.address: 115 Xinjiekou Beidajie (新街口北大街115号)
voyage.content: Beijing cuisine specialising in hot pot served in the traditional copper cone pots with coal.

voyage.name: Hot & Tasty
voyage.address: 西城区金城坊街9－7号
voyage.content: Sichuan cuisine as hot as you will find it in Sichuan.

voyage.name: Royal Icehouse
voyage.address: Gongjian Hutong
voyage.content: Beijing cuisine. The restaurant is in the former royal ice house.

voyage.name: Tong He Ju
voyage.address: B71 Yueyun South St (月云南街乙71号)
voyage.content: Shandong cuisine. This restaurant has been around for centuries. It is spacious with large tables.

voyage.name: Yu Guo Tian Qing
voyage.address: 35 Tonglingge Rd (佟麟阁路35号)
voyage.content: Beijing cuisine specialising in dumplings.

voyage.name: The Woods
voyage.alt: 北京阔海丽景餐饮管理有限公司
voyage.address: Seasons Place - 3rd Floor, Shop L301, Financial Street 北京市西城区金融街购物中心二期3F-301
voyage.content: Salads and sandwiches with good quality ingredients with a seating area in the open space area of a shopping mall

voyage.name: Await Café
voyage.address: 59 Xisi South Street 西四南大街59号
voyage.content: A true travellers café, with three floors, meals, drinks and desserts, filled with souvenirs from the four corners of the globe.

voyage.name: The Gourmet Room
voyage.address: 3 Qianhai West St (前海西街3号 Qiánhǎixījiē)
voyage.content: Hong Kong cuisine served in courtyard restaurant. Offers a classic 10-course menu.

voyage.name: Lijia Cai Restaurant
voyage.address: 11 Yangfang Hutong, Deshengmennei St (德胜门内大街羊房胡同11号 Déshèngménnèi Dàjiē Yáng​fáng Hú​tòng​)
voyage.content: Imperial cuisine. This is a small family run restaurant in a hutong. The set menus consist of ten cold dishes and eight hot. The dishes are small and quite simple, but very tasty. There are only three tables in the restaurant, so book in advance.

voyage.name: Haiqing Heyan
voyage.address: 2 Banqiao Santiao, Xihai Xiyan (西海西沿板桥3条2号 Xīhǎixīyàn Bǎn​qiáo​tiáo​)
voyage.content: Small courtyard restaurant serving French Teppanyaki. There are great views of the lake from the four private rooms. Modern and stylish decor. Reservations are needed.

voyage.name: Ken de Rouge
voyage.address: 22 Houhai West Bank (后海西沿22号 Hòuhǎixīyàn)
voyage.content: Modern Chinese cuisine. This is a romantic restaurant with views of the lake.

voyage.name: The Noble Restaurant/Bar
voyage.address: Bajiao Pavilion, Houhai Park (后海公园内八角亭 Hòuhǎi Gōngyuánnèi Bājiǎotíng)
voyage.content: Zhejiang-French fusion restaurant with views of the lake.

voyage.name: Fu Lin
voyage.address: 23 Bajiaoting Hutong (八角亭胡同23号 Bājiǎotínghútòng)
voyage.content: Zhejiang cuisine served ub courtyard restaurant with trees, pond and views of the lake.

voyage.name: Bhodi-Saki
voyage.address: 10-16 Heiyaochang Street
voyage.content: Located just north of Taoranting Park in the south west corner of Beijing, this isolated vegetarian restaurant is situated inside a series of old courtyards that house the restaurant and a small temple.

voyage.name: Jin Yang Restaurant
voyage.address: No.241, Zhushikou West Street
voyage.content: Jin Yang Restaurant serves Shaanxi cuisine. Four Star Restaurant.

voyage.name: Quanjude
voyage.price: Ducks cost ¥199 each and ¥99 for half a duck
voyage.address: 32 Qianmen Dajie (前门大街32号)
voyage.content: The oldest and most venerable of the roast duck restaurants. Quanjude is slipping these days, but its fame still brings many customers, mostly tourists eager for the classic experience. Quality varies by location. The most reputable of Quanjude's 14 branches is the listed Qianmen location, which has been rebuilt as part of the changes taking place in Qianmen Dajie. Other branches are at Hepingmen (south of the subway

voyage.name: Whampoa Club
voyage.address: 23A Jinrong St (金融大街甲23号 Jīn​róng Dà​jiē​jiǎ​)
voyage.content: Serves modern Chinese food based on the old traditions of Beijing cuisine.

voyage.name: Restaurant at 95
voyage.address: No.95 Fuchengmennei Street 西城区阜成门内大街95号
voyage.content: A modern palace with exquisite style and traditional imperial service. Suitable for small group dining.

voyage.name: 15 Qianhai Beiyan
voyage.address: 15 Qianhai Beiyan (前海北沿15号 Qiánhǎiběiyàn)
voyage.content: Both indoor and outdoor seating and good views of the lake.

voyage.name: Blue Lotus Club
voyage.address: 1 Shichahai, Xihaidongyan (什刹海西海东沿1号 Shíchàhǎixīhǎidōngyàn)
voyage.content: Kitch bar with Chinese live instrumental orchestra in the weekend.

voyage.name: Jiadingfang
voyage.address: 9 Lotus Ln, 51 W Dia'nmen (地安门西大街51号什刹海天荷坊9号 Dìānménxīdàjiē51háo, Shíchàhǎitiānhéfāng9háo)
voyage.content: Large place by the lake with a long list of drink and food. Live music every night, primarily unknown local bands.

voyage.name: Rive Gauche
voyage.address: 2 South Bank, Qianhai, Shichahai (什刹海前海南沿2号 Shíchàhǎi Qiánhǎi Nányàn)
voyage.content: Quiet cocktail bar.

voyage.name: 4corners
voyage.content: Only bar in the area that caters to younger expats. Home base for popular local band Tavey Lean & the Solid Gold Dream Machine. Vietnamese restaurant during the day.

voyage.name: Cigar Legends Bar
voyage.address: 3 Jincheng Fangjie (金城坊街3号 Jīn​chéng​fāng​jiē​)
voyage.content: Lounges primarily frequented by cigar smokers. First class interior with deep upholstered armchairs.

voyage.name: Lao She Teahouse
voyage.address: 3 Qianmen West Street (前门西大街3号 Qiánménxīdàjiē)
voyage.content: Large tea house from 1988 named after the writer, Lao She. Serves tea and traditional snack. Live performance every night with acrobatics, opera and other traditional art.

voyage.name: Baitayuan Guest House
voyage.alt: 白塔园青年旅馆 Báitǎyuán Qīngnián Lǚguǎn
voyage.price: Discounted rates for dorms from ¥40, doubles from ¥160, breakfast included
voyage.address: 20 Dachaye Hutong (大茶叶胡同20号; Dàcháyè Hútòng)
voyage.content: Traditional courtyard hotel located in a hutong. Internet, bicycle hire, safety boxes, fridge, laundry facilities and swimming pool available.

voyage.name: Beijing Houhai Courtyard Guest House
voyage.address: 14 Sanbulao Hutong
voyage.content: One of the most charming old-Beijing style courtyard inns, located in Sanbulao Hutong in Houhai, about 20 minutes walk from the subway. It is only 5 minutes by foot to the Houhai Lake. They provide free services such as tours of the hutongs, tea, wireless internet access, satellite TV & DVD access, usage of kitchen, baggage deposit. The staff speak enough English to get by, and there is parking as well. Internet on t

voyage.name: Beijing Join Inn
voyage.price: ¥30 dormitory bed, ¥160 double room, ¥180 triple room (seasonal pricing)
voyage.address: 14 Qinmao Hutong, Zhaodengyu Rd
voyage.content: This hostel is in the popular Xinjiekou district close to the city center. In one of Beijing's hutongs, the hostel is close to key bus and subway services, making sightseeing relatively simple. This place has a great family/chilled out vibe.

voyage.name: Beijing Zhongyou Hotel
voyage.price: Listed rates for doubles from ¥220, discounted from ¥163 including breakfast
voyage.address: Courtyard 1 Lane 2 Liupukang (六铺炕二巷1号院 Liùpūkàng èrxiàng yihàoyuàn)
voyage.content: Three-star hotel. Rooms (some quite small) with internet against surcharge. Business center, beauty salon, ticket office, laundry service, karaoke and table tennis available. Chinese restaurant, coffee shop and room service.

voyage.name: Garden Inn
voyage.alt: 岭南佳园连锁酒店 (北京西单店) Lǐngnánjiāyuánliánsuǒjiǔdiàn (Běijīngxīdāndiàn)
voyage.price: Listed rates for doubles from ¥219, discounted from ¥164; no breakfast available.
voyage.address: 95 Tonglinge Rd (佟麟阁路95号 Tónglíngélù)
voyage.content: Rooms with free internet. Ticket office available.

voyage.name: Red Lantern House
voyage.price: Dorms from ¥50, singles from ¥130, doubles from ¥160
voyage.address: 5 Zhengjue Hutong, Xinjie Kou
voyage.content: This hostel is spread over three buildings, but all have a good reputation. The "West Yard" is a beautiful courtyard house with indoor and outdoor areas for socialising. It has a great friendly atmosphere. The courtyard at this hostel's center is a great place to hang out, talk to new friends or just sit by yourself and read. Located in a hutong. They offer airport pickup for ¥160.

voyage.name: 365 Inn
voyage.price: Dorm beds from ¥30, double rooms from ¥180
voyage.address: 55 Dazhalan West Street (大栅栏西街55号 Dàzhàlánxījiē
voyage.content: Located in the middle of the tourist area west of Qianmen Pedestrian Street. Free internet available but not in the rooms.

voyage.name: Beijing Far East Youth Hostel
voyage.price: Dorm beds from ¥35, listed rates for doubles from ¥220, discounted from ¥174
voyage.address: 90 Tieshuxie Street (铁树斜街90号 Tiěshùxiéjiē)
voyage.content: Hotel in a traditional Chinese courtyard. During summertime you should book one week in advance.

voyage.name: Changgong Hotel
voyage.price: Dorm beds ¥35, a triple room is ¥210
voyage.content: One of the cheapest places in the Qianmen Hutong. It has traditional architecture and is just next door from Far East and Leo's. May be difficult to find on a map, and best located by asking.

voyage.name: Emperor Guest House
voyage.address: 11 Ying Tao Xie Jie, Qianmen, Beijing
voyage.content: A beautiful 200-year-old courtyard. Free wifi, tasty restaurant. Staff is wonderfully friendly and speaks pretty good English. Gets a bit cold later in the year, but beds are very comfy and thick quilts are provided. Lots of good bao shops within walking distance.

voyage.name: Feilongge Hotel
voyage.address: 10 Baizhifang West Street (白纸坊西街10号 Báizhǐfāngxījiē)
voyage.content: Rooms with aircon, coffee facilities and satellite TV. Meeting facilities, karaoke and beauty salon available. Restaurant with Sichuan and Lu cuisine.

voyage.name: Home Inn (Beiwei Road)
voyage.alt: 如家酒店 (北京北纬路店) Rújiājiǔdiàn (Běijīngběiwěilùdiàn)
voyage.price: Listed rates for doubles from ¥239, discounted from ¥214; breakfast ¥15
voyage.address: 11 Xijing Road (西经路11号 Xījīnglù)
voyage.content: Small rooms with free internet. Business center and ticket office. Chinese restaurant.

voyage.name: Jing Yi Shi Hotel
voyage.price: Twin room ¥150, ¥180, ¥220; internet access ¥10 per hour
voyage.address: Located between Leo hostel and Far East Y/H
voyage.content: The hotel is in traditional courtyard. The staff do not speak much English but are very friendly. There are two PCs available.

voyage.name: Leo's Hostel
voyage.content: A good alternative to the Far East and is just around the corner. It has a Playstation 2, an internet bar, free wi-fi in the lobby and bar, and more. It is well-known for its friendly English-speaking staff and lively bar atmosphere. One downside is the noise level of the bar late at night.

voyage.name: Qian Men Hostel
voyage.address: 33 Meishi Street Qianmen
voyage.content: Qian Men Hostel is conveniently located within 5 minute walking distance of Tiananmen Square. It offers both private and dorm style rooms. It has a dvd room, a cafe, and bar. It also offers tours to numerous places around Beijing. Bikes can be rented for ¥20 a day.

voyage.name: Shanglin Hostel
voyage.price: Discounted rates for dorms from ¥35, doubles from ¥140, without breakfast
voyage.address: 22 Shanxixiang (陕西巷22号 Shǎnxīxiàng)
voyage.content: Located just outside the tuoristy area west of Qianmen Pedestrian Street. Aircon, internet, laundry service and bike hire available. Restaurant and bar.

voyage.name: Bamboo Garden Hotel
voyage.alt: 竹园宾馆 Zhú Yuán Bīnguǎn
voyage.content: A stone's throw from Houhai, this is one of the most interesting hotels in Beijing. It located in a large complex of courtyards, was residence of Sheng Xuanhuai, a Qing Mandarin, and later was home to Kang Sheng, head of the secret police of Communist China.

voyage.name: Beijing HWA (Apartment) Hotel
voyage.address: 130 N Xidan Ave
voyage.content: This four-star hotel is near SOGO Department Store, Oriental Plaza, and Tiananmen Square. It offers air-conditioned rooms, each features a contemporary European design. It also has a Banquet hall that can accommodates 50 persons. You can also check out their rooftop garden, indoor swimming pool, and sauna.

voyage.name: Guang'an Hotel
voyage.price: Listed rates for doubles from ¥880; discounted from ¥358, including breakfast
voyage.address: (广安门内大街321号 Guǎngānménnèidàjiē)
voyage.content: Rooms with internet available against a surcharge. Bar, business center, gift shop, beauty salon, karaoke and chess/poker room available. Chinese restaurant.

voyage.name: ACFTU Hotel
voyage.alt: 北京中国职工之家饭店 Běijīngzhōng Guózhígōngzhījiā Fàndiàn
voyage.price: Listed rates for doubles ¥988-11,800, discounted rates ¥498-8,960, breakfast ¥55
voyage.address: 1 Zhenwumiao Rd, Fuxingmenwai St (复兴门外大街真武庙路1号 Fùxīngménwàidàjiē Zhēnwǔmiàolù)
voyage.content: Four star hotel with rooms with internet access against surcharge. Business center, gift shop, beauty salon, ticket office, disco, karaoke, pool, table tennis and fitness available. Chinese and Western restaurants, as well as coffee shop, bar and room service.

voyage.name: Jing Ding Hang
voyage.content: This is a real estate company that renovated several ancient houses in the legendary hutongs around Houhai Lake (just behind the Forbidden City and Tiananmen Square), and rented them out during the Olympics.

voyage.name: Presidential Plaza Hotel
voyage.address: No.9, Fuchengmen Wai Road 阜成门外大街甲9号
voyage.content: The hotel was built in 2000 and offers the latest in state-of-the-art facilities. There are 486 rooms: Deluxe Room, Superior Room, Suite, etc.

voyage.name: Golden Sun Commercial Hotel
voyage.alt: 金色夏日商务酒店 Jīnsè Xiàrì Shāngwù Jiǔdiàn
voyage.price: Listed rates for doubles from ¥888; discounted from ¥438, including breakfast
voyage.address: 85 Xibianmennei Street (西便门内大街85号 Xībiànménnèidàjiē)
voyage.content: Four star hotel with rooms with free internet, aircon, mini bar, fridge, safety box and satellite TV. Conference room, billiards, table tennis, gym, night club, karaoke, chess and cards room and sauna available. Seafood restaurant.

voyage.name: Shenzhen Hotel
voyage.address: 1 Guang An Men Wai Street, Xuanwu District
voyage.content: Enjoys a prime Xuanwu District location. Business and leisure facilities including banquet halls and function rooms.

voyage.name: Chairman Mao Memorial Hall
voyage.hours: Tue-Sun 08:00-12:00 (but it is sometimes closed without notice)
voyage.content: The body of the founder of the People's Republic of China, Mao Zedong, has been preserved (against his own wishes) and is on display in here. Expect huge, but moving, queues. No bags, cameras or water bottles are allowed inside and must be dropped off (for a fee) at the bag-check building across the road to the east (mobile phones are permitted). Flowers can be purchased to lay at the feet of Mao's statue inside (alt

voyage.name: Monument to the People's Heroes
voyage.content: A cenotaph with round-the-clock honor guard commemorating the PRC's veterans and war dead. Illuminated at night. Usually blocked off unless there is an important ceremony or visitors, but even then only those participating can go to the base of the cenotaph. However, you can usually get close enough to take pictures.

voyage.name: Great Hall of the People
voyage.content: The seat of the National People's Congress (NPC), China's unicameral legislature, as well as the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC), its main political advisory body. Both assemblies convene here once a year for about ten days in what is known as the "Two Sessions" (两会). Meetings of both assemblies take place in the Great Auditorium, with their times staggered to avoid conflicts. In addition t

voyage.name: Tian'anmen Gate
voyage.alt: 天安门; Gate of Heavenly Peace
voyage.content: Tian'anmen Gate, and its large portrait of Chairman Mao, dominates the northern end of the square. This was originally the main gate into the Imperial City, and is the only one of the four gates that still survives. Pass beneath the gate to head north toward the Forbidden City. It costs nothing to pass through, but on the far side there is a ticket booth where you can pay admission to visit the gate. Although visitin

voyage.name: Zhongshan Park
voyage.address: West side of Tian'anmen (天安门西侧; Tiānānménxīcè)
voyage.content: Beautifully landscaped park with lots of trees and bamboo. The Forbidden City, covered in a separate article, is entered through this park. Paddle boats for rent on the moat of the Forbidden City. Also an indoor playground for children, and bumper cars.

voyage.name: Zhengyangmen
voyage.content: Built in 1419 as the front gate of the inner city wall. It was only used by the emperor on his way to Tiantan. Now it houses exhibits with photos and models of the old city.

voyage.name: Zhihua Temple
voyage.alt: 智化寺; Zhìhuàsì; also known as Temple of Wisdom Attained
voyage.address: 5 Lumicang Hutong (禄米仓胡同5号; Lùmǐcānghútòng)
voyage.content: Buddhist temple built in 1443. One of the largest, oldest and best preserved wooden structures in Beijing. Houses the Ancient Music Center, which now and then gives concerts according to ancient traditions at 10:00 and 15:00. Also houses the Beijing Cultural Exchange Museum. It has been renovated. Free tour guide at 09:30 and 14:00.

voyage.name: Imperial Ancestral Temple
voyage.price: ¥2, does not include entry into buildings
voyage.content: This was the temple where the emperors and other members of the royal family would pay respect to their ancestors. The buildings are original, though much of the interior, including the ancestral tablets, were destroyed during the Cultural Revolution. It has since been repurposed as a museum dedicated to the working class Chinese.

voyage.name: Beijing Police Museum
voyage.alt: 北京警察博物馆; Běijīng Jǐngchá Bówùguǎn
voyage.hours: 09:00-16:00, no entry after 15:30, closed on Mondays
voyage.address: 36 Dongjiaomin Lane (东交民巷36号; Dōngjiāomín Xiàng)
voyage.content: Large museum on police history.

voyage.name: China Court Museum
voyage.alt: 中国法院博物馆; Zhōngguó Fǎyuàn Bówùguǎn
voyage.hours: 09:00-17:00, no entry after 16:00, closed on Mondays
voyage.address: 4 Zhengyi Road (正义路4号; Zhèngyì Lù)
voyage.content: A museum about the court system in China. The museum is in a historic building dating from 1910 that was originally the Beijing branch of the Yokohama Specie Bank, a Japanese bank.

voyage.name: China Customs Museum
voyage.alt: 中国海关博物馆; Zhōngguó Hǎiguān Bówùguǎn
voyage.hours: 09:00-16:30, no tickets issued after 15:45, no entry permitted after 16:00, closed on Mondays
voyage.address: 2 Jianguomen Inner Avenue (建国门内大街2号; Jiànguómén Nèi Dàjiē
voyage.content: A national-level museum run by the General Administration of Customs of the People's Republic of China.

voyage.name: China National Museum of Women and Children
voyage.alt: 中国妇女儿童博物馆; Zhōngguó Fùnǚ Értóng Bówùguǎn, Museum of Chinese Women and Children
voyage.address: 9 Beijige Road (北极阁路9号; Běijígé Lù
voyage.content: A museum exhibiting numerous cultural and historical artefacts related to women and children in China. Visitors are expected to make a booking on WeChat at least one day before visiting the museum. The museum's WeChat account may be found by searching "中国妇女儿童博物馆公众号".

voyage.name: Imperial City Art Museum
voyage.address: 9 Changpuheyan (菖蒲河沿9号; Chāngpúhéyàn)
voyage.content: The Imperial City was the Manchu city that surrounded the Forbidden City during the Qing dynasty. The museum's centrepiece is a scale model of the Forbidden & Imperial Cities. There are also displays on lifestyle, costumes, arts & crafts of the Qing imperial city. Occasionally hosts special exhibits that cost extra.

voyage.name: National Museum of China
voyage.alt: 中国国家博物馆 Zhōngguó Guójiā Bówùguǎn
voyage.price: Free; foreign visitors must show their passport
voyage.address: 16 East Chang'an St, (东长安街16马 Dōngcháng'ānjiē)
voyage.content: A huge museum containing the ancient and recent history of the Chinese nation. Modern history exhibit focuses on the successes of the Communist Party (and obviously not the negatives). Most exhibits have short English explanations.

voyage.name: Shijia Hutong Museum
voyage.alt: 史家胡同博物馆; Shíjiā Hútóng Bówùguǎn
voyage.address: 24 Shijia Hutong (史家胡同24号; Shíjiā Hútóng
voyage.content: A traditional courtyard residence that has been turned into a museum. There are exhibitions about the history of the hutong and the daily lives of the residents.

voyage.name: CourtYard Gallery
voyage.address: 53 Donganmen Dajie (东安门大街53号; Dōngānméndàjiē)
voyage.content: Founded in 1996. Exhibits emerging and mid-career artists working in a wide range of media.

voyage.name: Wan Fung Art Gallery
voyage.address: 136 Nanchizi Jie
voyage.content: Worth a peek if you're in the area. Housed in a side building in the courtyard of the Imperial Archives, which you can't go in, but is quite impressive. The courtyard itself is a quiet corner in an otherwise crowded area of the city.

voyage.name: Legation Quarter
voyage.content: The legation quarter was once, as its name suggests, home to Beijing's many foreign diplomatic missions. During the 1900 Boxer Rebellion, the diplomats and Chinese Christians who sought their protection held out here until a 55-day siege was broken by foreign forces coming over the city walls. The embassies have since moved to larger quarters elsewhere, but the buildings remain. Now occupied by various Chinese govern

voyage.name: Ancient Observatory
voyage.address: 2 Dongbiaobei Hutong (东裱褙胡同2号; Dōngbiǎobèihútòng)
voyage.content: The observatory, built in 1442, has been open to the public since 1983. Ancient star maps and instruments to watch stars can be seen here. Displays on the history of Chinese astronomy, and several large astronomical instruments set on top of an old watchtower of the city walls.

voyage.name: Chaonei No. 81
voyage.address: 81 Chaoyangmen Inner St, 朝阳门街道内81号
voyage.content: This abandoned, overgrown Baroque Revival complex, dating to the early 20th century, has acquired an international reputation as the best-known allegedly haunted house in China. According to residents of the nearby hutongs, even the Red Guards moved out after a few days, supposedly scared off by the ghost of a Kuomintang officer's mistress who hanged herself when he fled to Taiwan without her. It inspired the 2014 fi

voyage.name: Changpu River Park
voyage.content: Narrow strip of landscaped park along a small stream. Begins in the east near the Beijing hotel and runs almost to Tian'anmen Gate.

voyage.name: Capital Theater
voyage.address: 22 Wangfujing Street (王府井大街22号; Wángfǔjǐngdàjiē)
voyage.content: This theater is used by different theater groups, including Beijing People's Art Theater. Performances include both contemporary and classical Chinese plays.

voyage.name: Chang'an Grand Theater
voyage.address: 7 Jianguomennei Street (建国门内大街7号; Jiànguóménnèidàjiē)
voyage.content: Traditional Chinese performances with focus on Beijing Opera. Also has a shop with paintings and folk handicrafts.

voyage.name: China Children's Art Theater
voyage.address: 64 Donganmen Street (东安门大街64号; Dōngānméndàjiē)
voyage.content: Established in 1956. Stages children's plays.

voyage.name: Dongyuan Theater
voyage.address: Inside the Garden of Changpu River (菖蒲河公园内; Chāngpúhégōngyuánnèi)

voyage.name: Goldsail Concert Hall
voyage.address: 24 Wangfujing Street (24 Wangfujing Street (王府井大街24号; Wángfǔjǐngdàjiē)
voyage.content: Small concert hall without speakers. Suitable for chamber music also.

voyage.name: Hutong Cuisine Cooking School
voyage.address: 35 Dengcao Hutong (灯草胡同35号)
voyage.content: A few places around Nanluoguxiang now offer Chinese cooking classes. One such place, Hutong Cuisine, is run by an English-speaking chef in a small hutong home. Classes are small. Reservations are necessary. Optional market tours are also conducted before cooking classes commence.

voyage.name: New China Children's Store
voyage.alt: 新中国儿童用品商店; Xīnzhōngguóértóngyòngpǐnshāngdiàn
voyage.address: 168 Wangfujing Street (王府井大街168号; Wángfǔjǐngdàjiē)
voyage.content: Play center for children where the kids can catch goldfish, play in the gigantic sandpit or other. They also sell all kind of gear for children.

voyage.name: Wangfujing
voyage.content: Beijing's most famous shopping street, nowadays with mostly the same international brands and modern malls you will find anywhere else in the world. The street is pedestrianised for several blocks, making it pleasant to walk around. Several large malls in the area such as Oriental Plaza (see below) and Sun Dong An plaza. One useful shop is the Foreign Language Bookstore, at the northern end of the pedestrian area, wh

voyage.name: The Malls at Oriental Plaza
voyage.alt: 东方新天地 Dōngfāng Xīn Tiāndì
voyage.address: East of Tian'anmen Square, on Wangfujing
voyage.content: At one time this was the largest mall in Asia. Modern shopping mall is expensive but provides you with a lot of buying opportunities from diamonds, to real (affordable) DVDs, (international) music CDs and food. You can find lots of brands in Oriental Plaza, from high-end to low. Besides shopping, you also can eat here, from Western cuisine to traditional Chinese food.

voyage.name: Poetry Cafe
voyage.address: No 15 Nanchizi street Dongcheng District Beijing (南池子大街15号故宫东华门旁
voyage.content: A beautiful cafe with soul as its name "Poetry", is operated by a lovely young lady, who enjoys travel and photography, that she gathers a group of 'specialists' in those fields; thus, customers can get tonnes of information about travel and photography. Customers can enjoy a view of the Forbidden City over a perfectly brewed coffee.

voyage.name: Wangfujing Snack Street
voyage.content: Many stalls selling Beijing-style snacks, both sweet and savoury.

voyage.name: Donghuamen Night Market
voyage.content: The place to come for exotic snacks such as scorpions, starfish, and silkworm grubs. You can also buy more typical snacks like fried noodles, dumplings, and kebabs. More expensive than a "real" neighbourhood market, but still reasonably priced.

voyage.name: Oriental Dumpling King
voyage.address: 14 Chaoyangmen Nanxiaojie (朝阳门南小街14号楼; Cháoyángménnánxiǎojiē)
voyage.content: Cheap and delicious Dongbei (northeast) style dumplings. This is a chain, one of several around town. Their location in Harbin is recommended in several guidebooks, but if you're not going there you can get the same dumplings in Beijing. A few dozen different kinds, and can be boiled or fried. As with many dumpling places, order by weight: An order is usually two liang (èr liǎng) which is 100g, about 10-12 dumplings.

voyage.name: Donglaishun
voyage.address: 198 Wangfujing, Dong Dan,
voyage.content: This king of Beijing hotpot has been around since 1903. Founded by the Hui (ethnic Muslims), Donglaishun serves halal cuts of top-quality lamb and beef. Also serves cooked-by-chef dishes, including traditional Beijing sweets.

voyage.name: Wangfujing branch
voyage.address: 198 Wangfujing, Dajie (东城区王府井大街198号)
voyage.content: Subway: Line 1 to Wangfujing

voyage.name: Yuxin Sichuan Restaurant
voyage.content: One of the contenders in the ongoing competition for Beijing's best Sichuanese, Yuxin delivers on authenticity, flavor, and service. It's always busy, and always good.

voyage.name: Peking Chamber (Forbidden City branch)
voyage.alt: 四季民福烤鸭店（故宫店）Sìjìmínfú Kăoyā Diàn Gùgōng Diàn
voyage.address: 11 Nanchizi Dajie
voyage.content: A Peking roast duck restaurant featuring a view of the Forbidden City. Reservations suggested.

voyage.name: Dadong Duck Restaurant
voyage.alt: 大董烤鸭店 Dàdŏng Kăoyā Diàn
voyage.price: sea cucumber ¥200-600, lobster from ¥200, +10% service charge
voyage.address: Three locations in Dongcheng district
voyage.content: Considered by some to be the best Peking duck in the city, this upscale restaurant also delivers on a nice atmosphere. Reservations suggested. full/half Peking duck is ¥240/120 with extra ¥8 for condiments. Meal is served with free hot water, small soup, light fruits and black sesame for dessert.

voyage.name: Earl Bar
voyage.address: 1 Dongdan North Street (东单北大街1号; Dōngdānběidàjiē)
voyage.content: Very basic bar with local DJs.

voyage.name: Beijing City Central Youth Hostel
voyage.price: Dorms ¥60 (4-8 beds), doubles with shared bathrooms ¥160
voyage.address: 1-5 Beijing Station West St. (北京站西街1-5号; Běijīngzhàn xījiē
voyage.content: The largest hostel in Beijing, with central air conditioning and individual controls in each of the 200 rooms. It offers a computer/internet room, billiards, bar, and karaoke. On the 1st and 2nd levels are a 24-hour supermarket, breakfast bar, coffee lounge, ATM, phones for international dialing, express film processing, a mobile phone shop, and post office. The rooms on the 3rd to 6th floors include ensuites, double

voyage.name: Beijing Saga International Youth Hostel
voyage.alt: 北京实佳国际青年旅舍; Běijīng Shíjiā Guójìqīngniánlǚshè
voyage.address: 9 Shijia Hutong, Nanxiao Street (南小街史家胡同9号; Nánxiǎojiē Shǐjiāhútòng)
voyage.content: Very popular with backpackers. There's a restaurant on the top floor. The staff speak some English.

voyage.name: Eastern Morning Youth Hostel
voyage.price: Private rooms cost about ¥90 per night—book in advance
voyage.address: Dongdan Santiao, behind the Oriental Plaza
voyage.content: A great budget option if price is your primary concern. The staff do not speak much English but are friendly. Internet access is available at ¥10 per hour. It is a 5-minute walk to the Dongdan or Wangfujing subway stations and about a 15-minute walk to the International Hotel airport shuttle stop.

voyage.name: Purple Courtyard
voyage.price: Price example, ¥408 for a triple room
voyage.address: no.24 Shajing Hutong, NanLuoGuXiang, Dongcheng
voyage.content: Wonderful location in a hutong, surrounded by a mass of eateries and a couple of mini-markets. Five-minute walk to buses and Shichahai metro, 10-minute walk to Nanluoguxiang metro. Bustling area but a five-minute walk from a complex of lakes. Friendly English-speaking staff who are always available to help. TV in Chinese, free Wi-Fi, private facilities, A/C and use of fridge freezer, which is important in the Beijing

voyage.name: Wangfujing Dawan Hotel
voyage.alt: 北京王府井大万酒店; Běijīngwángfǔjǐngdàwànjiǔdiàn
voyage.price: Listed rates for doubles from ¥238, discounted from ¥137; breakfast ¥15
voyage.address: 2 Ganyu Hutong, Dongdan Bei Street (东单北大街甘雨胡同甲2号; Dōngdānběidàjiēgānyǔhútòng)
voyage.content: Rooms with free Internet, television, a/c and fridge. Business center and bath center including sauna available. Chinese restaurant. The rooms are alright, the bathrooms not too bright or clean, and the service level fluctuates, but the low price and great location make up for it.

voyage.name: Beijing Fuhao Hotel
voyage.price: Rates for doubles on official website from ¥364.47
voyage.address: 45 Wangfujing Avenue (王府井大街45号; Wáng fǔ jǐngdà jiē)
voyage.content: The hotel offers 104 air-conditioned rooms with mini-bar, cable TV, free internet and fridge. Among its facilities are Lao Chongqing Hot-pot City Restaurant, Wangfujing Roast Duck Restaurant, a sauna club, and a night club/KTV.

voyage.name: Beijing Golden Palace Silver Street
voyage.alt: 北京金府银街大酒店; Běijīngjīnfǔyínjiēdàjiǔdiàn
voyage.price: Listed rates for doubles without window from ¥588, discounted from ¥172, rooms with window somewhat more expensive; western breakfast ¥20
voyage.address: 31 Ganyu Hutong, Wangfujing Street (王府井大街甘雨胡同31号; Wángfǔjǐngdàjiē Gānyǔhútòng
voyage.content: Rooms with internet access against surcharge as well as aircon, mini bar and safe. Cheapest rooms and bathrooms are quite small and not too clean. Business center, karaoke, beauty salon, gym and rooftop garden available. Chinese and Western restaurant and a coffee shop.

voyage.name: Beijing Harmony Hotel
voyage.address: 59 Suzhou Hutong, Youtong Street
voyage.content: International 3-star hotel with 3 minutes walk to the Beijing Railway Station and Dongdan Shopping street. Convenient location for tourists.

voyage.name: Dongjiao Minxiang Hotel
voyage.address: 23A Dongjiao Minxiang, 北京东城区东交民巷甲23号
voyage.content: Offers rooms with private toilet and bath with tub, slippers, bathrobe, and hair dryer.

voyage.name: The Emperor Beijing Forbidden City Hotel
voyage.alt: 北京故宫皇家驿栈酒店, Beijing gùgōnghuángjiā yìzhàn jiǔdiàn
voyage.address: 33 Qihelou St. 东城区骑河楼大街33号
voyage.content: Boutique hotel in residential neighborhood near Forbidden City. Interestingly designed rooms are named after emperors rather than numbered. Free breakfast from rooftop restaurant with sweeping views over the Forbidden City. Long walk to subway stations.

voyage.name: Wancheng Hua Fu International Hotel
voyage.alt: 北京万程华府国际酒店
voyage.price: ¥338 for a single room. Breakfast buffet available for ¥20
voyage.address: 53 Donganmen Street, 北京东城区东安门大街53号
voyage.content: Rather basic rooms, but clean with nice bathroom and TV (Chinese channels). Some staff had trouble speaking English but all were friendly. Excellent location close to Wangfujing shopping area, 10 min walk to Forbidden City.

voyage.name: Jingyuan Courtyard Hotel - Beijing
voyage.address: 35 Xitangzi Hutong, Wangfujing Street
voyage.content: Rooms are air-conditioned and fitted with a full bath, mini-bar, cable TV, and Internet access.

voyage.name: Tangyue Hotel
voyage.price: Listed rates for doubles from ¥580, discounted from ¥207; western breakfast ¥25
voyage.address: 54 Donghuamen Road (东华门大街54号; Dōnghuàméndàjiē)
voyage.content: Spacious rooms with free internet, fridge, safe and coffee facilities. Specially designed hotel with business center, beauty salon, ticket office available. Coffee shop with first-class coffee, bar and tea house but no restaurant.

voyage.name: Beijing Hotel Nuo
voyage.alt: 北京饭店诺金; Běijīng Fàndiàn Nuòjīn
voyage.address: 33 East Chang'an Ave. (东长安街33号, Dōngcháng'ānjiē)
voyage.content: Housed in the historic French-built Block B of the former Grand Hôtel de Pékin that was completed in 1917, and the newer and more modern Block E that was completed in 2001, this is the oldest hotel in Beijing. The 1917 building is in a beautiful French Beaux-Arts architectural style.

voyage.name: Grand Hotel Beijing
voyage.alt: 北京贵宾楼饭店; Běijīng Guìbīnlóu Fàndiàn
voyage.price: Listed rates for doubles ¥3,450-14,950, discounted rates ¥765-10,500, breakfast ¥184
voyage.address: 35 East Chang'an Street (东长安街35号; Dōngchángānjiē)
voyage.content: Housed in the 1954-built Block C of the former Grand Hôtel de Pékin, built in a fusion of Stalinist and traditional Chinese architectural styles.

voyage.name: Grand Hyatt Beijing
voyage.alt: 北京东方君悦大酒店; Běijīng dōngfāng jūnyuè dàiǔdiàn
voyage.address: 1 East Chang'an Avenue (东长安街1号, Dōngcháng'ānjiē
voyage.content: Privately-owned, exquisite, and expensive 5-star hotel. There is an enormous swimming pool in the basement that is decorated in very tropical manner, but the deepest part is only 1.5 m (5 ft). The jacuzzi and wet sauna are excellent. Great hotel and great location, if you can afford it.

voyage.name: Legendale Hotel Beijing
voyage.alt: 北京励骏酒店; Běijīng Lìjùn Jiǔdiàn
voyage.price: Listed rates for doubles ¥4,140-7,820, discounted rates ¥1,478-5,797
voyage.address: 90-92 Jinbao Street (金宝街90-92号; Jīnbǎojiē)
voyage.content: Five-star hotel located close to Wangfujing. Rooms of 38-71 m² with free Internet. Business center, beauty salon, karaoke, fitness, swimming pool, massage and sauna available. Chinese and Western restaurants, coffee shop and bar.

voyage.name: Regent Beijing
voyage.alt: 北京丽晶酒店;Běijīng lì jīng jiǔdiàn
voyage.address: 99 Jinbao St, Dong Dan, Dongcheng, Beijing, China, 100005
voyage.content: Large luxury hotel with buffet breakfast, an indoor pool, a spa, and fitness center.

voyage.name: The Peninsula Beijing
voyage.alt: 北京王府半岛酒店; Běijīng Wángfǔbàndǎo Jiǔdiàn
voyage.price: Listed rates for doubles from ¥3,400, discounted from ¥1,500, breakfast ¥299
voyage.address: 8 Jinyu Hutong, Wangfujing (王府井金鱼胡同8号; Wángfǔjǐng Jīnyúhútòng)
voyage.content: Five-star hotel with rooms with free internet. The smallest rooms are 31 m². Swimming pool, spa, massage and lots of shops available. Chinese and Western restaurants as well as a bar.

voyage.name: Xinhai Jin Jiang Hotel
voyage.alt: 鑫海锦江大酒店; Xīnhǎi jǐnjiāng dàjiǔdiàn
voyage.address: 61 Jinbao Street (金宝街61号, Jīnbǎojiē)
voyage.content: In the bustling commercial district of Wangfujing, this hotel has 231 elegantly furnished rooms. It has excellent business and leisure facilities which include the sprawling International Conference Center.

voyage.name: Badachu
voyage.alt: 八大处; Bādàchǔ; lit. The Eight Great Sites
voyage.content: Badachu is comprised of eight Buddhist temples and monasteries at the foot of the Western Hills. Restored in the 1980s, the whole area is now a park and popular tourist destination for Beijingers wishing to escape city life.

voyage.name: Hope Park
voyage.content: A small but attractive park south-east of Badachu.

voyage.name: Fahai Temple
voyage.content: This 15th-century temple has some of the best-preserved and extensive Ming frescoes to be found.

voyage.name: Tianyi's Tomb
voyage.address: 80 Moshikou Dajie (模式口大街80号)
voyage.content: This is the most extensive and well-preserved Ming dynasty tomb of a eunuch. There is a Eunuch Culture Museum (¥8 entrance fee) at the same site.

voyage.name: Cheng'en Temple
voyage.address: East Moshikou Dajie (模式口大街东部)
voyage.content: This is another temple with a history of at least five hundred years.

voyage.name: China Quaternary Glacier Museum
voyage.alt: 中国第四纪冰川陈列馆; Zhōngguó Dìsìjì Bīngchuān Chénlièguǎn
voyage.address: Moshikou Dajie (模式口大街)
voyage.content: This museum was founded in 1992 and offers an introduction to geology, geography, and glaciers.

voyage.name: Beijing International Sculpture Park
voyage.alt: 北京国际雕塑公园 Běijīng Guójì Diāosù Gōngyuán
voyage.content: Opened in 2002, this park places sculpture from around the world in an attractive, green setting.

voyage.name: Babaoshan Revolutionary Cemetery
voyage.alt: 八宝山革命公墓; Bābǎoshān Gémìng Gōngmù
voyage.content: Built as a temple, it was made into the chief cemetery for Communist Party figures. Buried here are artist Xu Feihong, writer Lao She, and many of the most important CCP leaders.

voyage.name: Cishan Temple
voyage.alt: 天泰山慈善寺; Tiāntàishān Císhàn Sì
voyage.content: This is also known as Tiantai Temple. You will be lucky to see this one: the temple only opens March 15–17 of every year.

voyage.name: Shougang Industry Heritage Park tour
voyage.alt: 首钢工业旅游; Shǒugāng Gōngyè Lǚyóu
voyage.content: A former steel production complex converted into an industrial heritage and cultural site. Guided tours explain the steel-making process and the history of the complex. Part of the former plant has been transformed into So Real, an intergalactic station-themed attraction where cosplayers gather. The blast furnace area is worth visiting during the day, but is particularly atmospheric at night, when the immense scale a

voyage.name: Wanda Plaza
voyage.content: Shopping mall.

voyage.name: 工人 bar
voyage.content: Upstairs bar overlooking the Shougang steelworks, located across the street west of the blast furnaces. The house specialty is the "Blast Furnace", a spicy cocktail featuring a generous dose of Tabasco sauce.

voyage.name: Super 8 Hotel (Beijing Shijingshan Wanda Plaza Taiwan Street Branch)
voyage.alt: 速8精选酒店(北京石景山万达广场台湾街店)
voyage.address: Building 74 South Side, Yongle East District, Lugu East Street, Shijingshan District, Beijing, 100040, China
voyage.content: A budget hotel renovated in 2025. Strong guest ratings for cleanliness and value.

voyage.name: Mercure Wanshang Beijing
voyage.alt: 北京万商花园酒店 Běijīng Wànshāng Huāyuán Jiǔdiàn
voyage.address: No. 1 Yinhe Street (银河大街1号 Yínhé Dàjiē), Shijingshan District
voyage.content: Accor-operated hotel near Shijingshan Amusement Park and Wanda Plaza. Facilities include an indoor swimming pool, gym, indoor tennis court, billiards room, garden, business centre, meeting rooms, restaurant, café and free parking.

voyage.name: Wanda Realm Beijing
voyage.alt: 北京万达嘉华酒店 Běijīng Wàndá Jiāhuá Jiǔdiàn
voyage.address: Building 1, No. 18 Jia Shijingshan Road (石景山路甲18号1号楼)
voyage.content: Upscale business hotel in the Wanda Plaza complex. Spacious rooms and suites with city or Western Hills views. Facilities include indoor swimming pool, executive lounge, fitness centre, conference facilities, concierge service, currency exchange, and multiple restaurants offering Chinese, Japanese, and international cuisine.

voyage.name: Shangri-La Shougang Park
voyage.content: An unusual luxury hotel integrated into the former power plant of the Shougang steelworks. The industrial architecture has been incorporated into the hotel, while Power Station, the lobby restaurant and bar, is one of the most interesting hotel dining spaces at a contemporary five star hotel.

voyage.name: Old Summer Palace
voyage.address: 28 Qinghua West Road 清华西路28号
voyage.content: Built in the 18th and early 19th centuries, these gardens were home to the emperors and Qing court. They were looted and destroyed in 1860 on the orders of Lord Elgin, head of an Anglo-French expedition to Beijing; the French protested the order but made sure to get their share of the loot. Many see this as yet another example of the evils of imperialism. The Chinese government continues to maintain it in a ruined st

voyage.name: Summer Palace
voyage.content: Extensive gardens and palaces constructed by the Qing emperors that are a , regarded as one of China's Four Great Gardens. In 1860, British and French soldiers damaged much of what was then known as the "Garden of Clear Ripples", but the area would be rebuilt and renamed by the Empress Dowager Cixi, using funds intended for modernizing the Qing navy. To arrive, take the 4 subway to Beigongmen. This is adjacent to the

voyage.name: Wall of Khanbaliq
voyage.content: Khanbaliq translates as "the khan's camp"; it was the capital of the Yuan Dynasty. It was a substantial city even in Yuan times (see Marco Polo's late 13th century description), and later grew into Beijing, but nearly all Beijing's important buildings were built by later dynasties.

voyage.name: Linglong Pagoda and the Linglong Park
Beijing World Art Museum
voyage.content: Art museum with calligraphy and other paintings. Check the China Millennium Monument, the huge sundial on top with great views.

voyage.name: Haidian Museum
voyage.address: 1-28 Zhongguancun Street (中关村大街28-1号)

voyage.name: Military Museum of the Chinese People's Revolution
voyage.alt: 中国人民革命军事博物馆 Zhōngguó Rénmín Gémìng Jūnshì Bówùguǎn
voyage.address: 9 Fuxing Lu 海淀区复兴路9号
voyage.content: A great place to read the official Chinese version of what happened in Chinese military history, from ancient times up to 1949. There are also airplanes, boats, guns, missiles, rockets and vehicles on display (including U.S. military hardware evidently seized during the Korean conflict). You can pay an extra ¥5 to take a picture in a 1980s era Chinese tank. Very few signs are translated to English.

voyage.name: Art Museum of Tsinghua University
voyage.hours: 09:00-17:00, no entry after 16:30, closed on Mondays and during the Spring Festival
voyage.address: Qinghua University, 30 Shuangqing Road (双清路30号清华大学)

voyage.name: The Museum of Ethnic Cultures of the Minzu University of China
voyage.alt: 中央民族大学民族博物馆
voyage.hours: Mon-Thu 09:00-17:00, except for public holidays and university vacation periods
voyage.address: Minzu University of China, 27 Nanda Street, Zhongguan Village (中关村南大街27号中央民族大学校园内)

voyage.name: Art Gallery (and Library) of China National Academy of Painting
voyage.address: 54 Xi San Huan North Road (西三环北路54号)
voyage.content: Besides painting, there's an old Huizhou Building (w:Huizhou,_Anhui#Architecture) moved from Anhui to here. Huizhou is not easy to visit so this may be. Visitors are required to make an appointment before visiting.

voyage.name: Arthur M. Sackler Museum of Art and Archaeology at Peking University
voyage.alt: 北京大学赛克勒考古与艺术博物馆
voyage.address: 5 Yiheyuan Road (颐和园路5号)

voyage.name: Geological Museum of Peking University
voyage.address: 5 Yiheyuan Road (颐和园路5号)
voyage.content: Visitors are required to make a booking before visiting the museum.

voyage.name: Memorial of Famous Generals in the War of Resistance Against Japanese Agression
voyage.address: 18 Xiangshanbeizhenghuangqi (香山北正黄旗18号)
voyage.content: Dedicated to the Chinese generals who fought the Japanese during World War II. See World War II in China for context.

voyage.name: China National Botanical Garden
voyage.alt: 国家植物园 Guójiā Zhíwù Yuán "Municipal Garden", "Northern Garden"
voyage.content: Steps away from the east gate of Fragrant Hill. Acres of greenery and flowers for those tired of urban smog and traffic noise. Sir Johnston, teacher of the last emperor Puyi, had a villa in Cherry Glen, a silent and beautiful retreat in the Gardens. In the spring, the gardens hosts special exhibits of tulips, peach and plum blossoms, peonies, and the like. Separated by the Fragrant Hill Road, the North garden is the

voyage.name: Cherry Valley Forest of Red Dawnwoods
voyage.price: Part of the municipal Botanical Garden

voyage.name: Fragrant Hills
voyage.content: A good place for weekend outings and picnics. Formerly a Qing imperial garden, today Fragrant Hills makes an easy short climb in the suburbs of Beijing. It's also home to the Fragrant Hills Hotel, designed by noted architect I.M. Pei (Louvre Museum Pyramid).

voyage.name: Purple Bamboo Park
voyage.address: 45 Baishiqiao Road (白石桥路45号 Báishíqiáolù)
voyage.content: One of the larger parks in Beijing, this is centered around three lakes. As the name indicates, there is an outstanding variety of bamboo groves here. A superb place for a stroll and, since it's a favorite spot for locals to relax and exercise, a splendid opportunity to get away from the tourist draws and experience ordinary life in Beijing.

voyage.name: Yuyuantan Park
voyage.alt: 玉渊潭公园; Yùyuāntán Gōngyuán; also known as Jade Lake Park
voyage.address: Sanlihe Road, West Ring Road Three (西三环路三里河路 Xīsānhuánlù Sānlǐhélù)
voyage.content: Huge park with cherry blossoms, tulips, lake with boats for rent, water park and playgrounds. Popular for picnic or kite flying.

voyage.name: Fenghuangling
voyage.content: mountain with nice rock view; lots of wild walnuts (on the ground) to during the fall.

voyage.name: Yangtaishan
voyage.content: just mountain

voyage.name: Jiufeng
voyage.content: A 465-m hill shaped like a vulture.

voyage.name: Bussière Garden
voyage.address: Bei'anhe Village
voyage.content: A Chinese garden built by French physician Jean Jérôme Augustin Bussière in 1923, which is now a Sino-French cultural communication center.

voyage.name: Sikeshu/Biesimao
voyage.price: Free if visit from Taizhouwu (太舟坞); not if visit from Beijing Botanical Garden
voyage.content: Pear and peach blossoms during the spring season.

voyage.name: Baiwangshan Forest Park
voyage.alt: 百望山森林公园 (Bǎiwàngshān Sēnlín Gōngyuán), Mt. Baiwang
voyage.content: Small forest park, but close to the city, and not crowded.

voyage.name: Five Pagoda Temple
voyage.alt: 五塔寺 Wǔtǎ Sì, also known as Zhenjue Temple
voyage.address: 24 Waitaisi Cun, Baishiqiao 白石桥五塔寺村24号
voyage.content: The "Five Pagoda Temple" is the popular name of the Diamond-Throne Tower that is at the heart of the Temple of the Great Righteous Awakening (大真觉寺 Dàzhēnjiào Sì). Most of the wooden temple was burnt down in 1860 and 1900, but the beautiful brick and marble Diamond-Throne Tower, which dates back to the late fifteenth century, survived. The temple area is now used to house the Beijing Art Museum of Stone Carvings. Righ

voyage.name: Great Bell Temple & Museum
voyage.alt: 大钟寺古钟博物馆 Dàzhōng Sì Gǔzhōng Bówùguǎn
voyage.price: ¥30, free for the first 200 people on Wednesday
voyage.content: Also known as the Temple of Awakening Life (觉生寺 Juéshēng Sì). Home to the 15th-century Yongle Great Bell which, at 6.94 m tall and 46.5 tons, is the largest bell in China. The 227,000 Chinese characters inscribed on it spell out Buddhist sutras. Subway Line 13 to Dazhongsi, and then walk 400 m west.

voyage.name: Wanshou Temple
voyage.address: Xihuan Huanbeilu 西环环北路
voyage.content: Built in 1577, this Ming-era temple now houses the Beijing Art Museum (北京艺术博物馆 Běijīng Yìshù Bówùguǎn), which has a sizable collection of ancient artwork. Just north-west of Purple Bamboo Park; from Xizhimen take Bus 362 to Purple Bamboo Bridge North (紫竹桥北 Zǐzhú Qiáo Běi).

voyage.name: Qinghe Mosque
voyage.content: traditional Chinese-style mosque

voyage.name: Longquan Monastery
voyage.content: It is still active with monks and volunteers. Do not expect to see anything old, as most cultural relics are generally not allowed to have active Buddhist religious activities such as incense-burning for building preservation reason.

voyage.name: Dajue Temple
voyage.content: A 15th century Ming Dynasty temple famous for its Yulan magnolia.

voyage.name: Tsinghua University
voyage.content: Tsinghua University, one of the top universities in China, is essentially a tiny city. Walls separate the university from the city outside, and most of the students, staff and faculty live in the campus. The campus was part of the Old Summer Palace and there are lots of greens and a lake. In addition to the facilities of most other universities, there are grocery markets, banks, two post offices, one hospital, and a

voyage.name: Central TV Tower
voyage.price: ¥90 for admission ticket; ¥258 for lunch at the revolving restaurant; ¥308 for dinner at the revolving restaurant
voyage.address: 11 West 3rd Ring Rd Central
voyage.content: A tower with an observation deck at the height of 238 meters, providing a view of central Beijing. Below the observation deck is a dedicated television cultural center at 235 m, with a virtual television studio scene. A revolving restaurant at 221 meters provides both food and scenery.

voyage.name: Nanchanghe Trail East
voyage.content: Not connected to the west section - break at the Beijing-Kalgan high speed railway

voyage.name: Nanchanghe Trail West
voyage.content: Not connected to the east section - break at the Beijing-Kalgan high speed railway

voyage.name: Sujiatou III and IV village
voyage.content: A typical northern Chinese village reminiscent of the 1980s. Not recommended unless you have a "special interest" in it. The villagers are expecting that the village can be demolished in the near future.

voyage.name: Changlecun
voyage.content: A typical Haidian pond village. Not recommended unless you have a special interest in it.

voyage.name: Tour the University District
