voyage.content: Peking and Tsinghua universities are the two most prestigious in China, and have attractive campuses next to one another at the center of Beijing's university district. Limited tickets are available for the public to visit the campuses on weekends and summer holidays, but must be reserved in advance; like with any other tourist attractions in China, tickets are tied to your ID, so do not buy tickets from the scalpers

voyage.name: Read about China at the National Library
voyage.address: 33 Zhongguancun Nadajie 海淀区中关村南大街33号
voyage.content: The National Library has a large collection of books in English about China. Day-passes can be obtained for a small fee.

voyage.name: Haidian Theater
voyage.address: 28 Zhongguancun Dajie, 中关村大街28号
voyage.content: Modern theater with quality equipment, holding a large 1000-seat hall as well as two smaller halls. Foreign movies are usually screened in the respective language with Chinese subtitles. Besides movies there are various other performances, including concerts, opera, ballet, dance, plays and more.

voyage.name: Cruise from Beijing Exhibition Center to the Summer Palace
Golden Resources Shopping Mall
voyage.alt: 金源时代购物中心 Jīnyuán Shídài Gòuwù Zhōngxīn
voyage.address: near Yuanda Bridge / Yuanda Road off the West Fourth Ring Road in Haidian District
voyage.content: The mall covers 680,000 m², and is the second largest in Asia. Multiple stories, snaking alleys, infinite shopping opportunities... you get the gist.

voyage.name: New Wudaokou Clothing Market
voyage.address: 2 Qinghua Donglu, Golden Tower, 清华东路2号 金码大厦
voyage.content: 4-storey market packet with clothing, footwear and accessorizes, especially popular with students from nearby universities. A lot of Korean and Japanese style fashion. Staff is not pushing, drinks/snacks are available on the top floor.

voyage.name: Wudaokou Clothing Market
voyage.address: 261 Beisihuan Zhonglu, 北四环中路261号

voyage.name: Zhongguancun
voyage.content: For the more technologically-oriented tourist, is a must. Located directly south from Peking University and Tsinghua University (and accessible from Line 4 on the subway), this area is dubbed the "Silicon Valley of China." There are a number of large electronics malls that sell everything from phones to computer parts. Food is also abundant in the area, especially in recently-renovated urban zones. Pirated software a

voyage.name: Hailong
voyage.address: 1 Zhongguancun Dajie, 中关村大街1号

voyage.name: Dinghao
voyage.address: 3 Haidian dajie, 海淀大街3号

voyage.name: Zhongguancun Innovation Street
voyage.alt: formerly Haidian Book City, 海淀图书城 Hǎi​diàn​tú​shū​chéng
voyage.address: 36 Haidian Xidajie, 海淀西大街36号

voyage.name: Zhongguancun Book Building
voyage.alt: 中关村图书大厦 Zhōng​guān​cūn tú​shū dà​shà
voyage.address: 68 Beisihuan Xilu, 北四环西路68号

voyage.name: Beijing Language and Culture University Press Store
voyage.alt: 北京语言大学出版社 Běi​jīng yǔ​yán dà​xué chū​bǎn​shè
voyage.content: One of the best stores to buy language learning books.

voyage.name: Carrefour
voyage.address: Zhongguancun Plaza, 中关村广场地
voyage.content: Cheap French supermarket chain, selling everything from food, homeware, clothing to DVDs and electrical appliances. A bit pricier is their import section, offering food products from all over the world.

voyage.name: Wal Mart
voyage.address: 48 Zhichunlu, 知春路甲48号

voyage.name: Dong Lai Shun
voyage.content: This king of Beijing hotpot has been around since the 19th century. Founded by the Hui (ethnic Muslims), Donglaishun serves halal cuts of top-quality lamb and beef. Also serves cooked-by-chef dishes, including traditional Beijing sweets.

voyage.name: Haidian branch
voyage.address: 25 Yiheyuan Lu, 颐和园路25号, Haidian

voyage.name: Din Tai Fung Restaurant
voyage.address: 40 Zhongguancun Dajie, 中关村大街40号
voyage.content: Famous Shanghai-style dumplings restaurant.

voyage.name: Tairyo Teppanyaki
voyage.alt: 大渔铁板烧 Dà Yú Tiě​bǎnshāo
voyage.address: 15 Wan Liu Zhong Lu, 万柳中路15号
voyage.content: Japanese Teppanyaki grill show. All you can eat offer for ¥300.

voyage.name: Jardin de Jade
voyage.address: North Bldg, Block C, Ronge Information Centre, 2 Academy Rd

voyage.name: Isshin Japanese Restaurant
voyage.alt: 一心日本料理 Yīxīn Rìběn Liàolǐ
voyage.address: Courtyard of 35 Chengfu Lu 成府路35号院
voyage.content: An inexpensive and tasty Japanese restaurant that is packed most nights. 25 m north-west of the Wudaokou subway station in a small courtyard.

voyage.name: Jiaheyipin Congee Restaurant
voyage.address: 35 Chengfu Lu 成府路35号
voyage.content: Branches of this excellent congee restaurant can be found across Beijing. This one is just west of the Wudaokou subway station.

voyage.name: Ganges Indian Restaurant
voyage.address: 160 Chengfu Lu, 成府路160号

voyage.name: Dog Restaurant
voyage.address: 5th floor Youyi Shopping City

voyage.name: Sugar Shack
voyage.address: Basement, Huaqing Jiayuan #12, Chengfu Rd 海淀区成府路华清嘉园12号楼B1
voyage.content: Pizza restaurant and a haven for students

voyage.name: Tianchumiaoxiang Vegetarian
voyage.address: Tsinghua University Sicence Park 海淀区清华科技园创业大厦110室
voyage.content: The best in vegetarian cuisine following Buddhist traditions

voyage.name: Yummy Box
voyage.address: 3rd floor Hua Qing Jia Yuan Dongmen, Wudaokou Haidian
voyage.content: A great restaurant to visit, if you would like the taste of American style pizza.

voyage.name: Xinjiang Bayingolin Jinsite Restaurant
voyage.alt: 新疆巴州金丝特餐厅 "Xinjiang Bazhou Jinsite"
voyage.address: 2 Zaojunmiao, Sidaokou Road, Haidian, Beijing (皂君庙2号巴州驻京联络办内)
voyage.content: Genuine Oirat Mongolian food.

voyage.name: Sculpting in Time
voyage.content: Laid-back cafe with free wifi and a small menu of food. Popular with both locals and foreigners. They now have eight branches across Beijing.

voyage.name: Wudaokou Branch
voyage.address: Fl. 2, Building 12, Huaqing Jiayuan 成府路华清嘉园12 号楼2 号3-4F
voyage.content: South-west of the Wudaokou subway station.

voyage.name: Fragrant Hills Branch
voyage.address: 50 Maimai Rd, Fragrant Hills 香山买卖街50号
voyage.content: Just a little east from the main gate of the Fragrant Hills.

voyage.name: Lush
voyage.address: Level 2, Bld. 1, Huaqing Jiayuan, Wudaokou 五道口华清家园1号楼2层
voyage.content: A very popular foreign student hangout, this bar has a pub quiz on Wednesdays and an open-mic night on Sundays.

voyage.name: Propaganda
voyage.content: Just south of Lush & Sculpting in Time, this bar/club is packed on weekends, with a mix of mainly Korean, Japanese, and Western students. Wednesday nights are all-you-can-drink for ¥80 or so (the price constantly changes, and it's lower if you're female).

voyage.name: PekingUni International Youth Hostel
voyage.alt: 北京未名国际青年旅舍; Běijīng Wèimíng Guójìqīngniánlǚshè
voyage.price: Discounted rates for dorms (a bed in a shared room)/doubles without bathroom/doubles with bathroom from ¥60-410 without breakfast
voyage.address: 150 Chengfu Road (成府路150号 Chéngfǔlù)
voyage.content: Right smack in the university district, closest hostel to Olympic area. Free internet, guest kitchen and bike hire available. Restaurant and bar.

voyage.name: Huayetianyuan Hotel
voyage.alt: 北京天缘惠达宾馆 (原华业天缘宾馆); Běijīngtiānyuánhuìdábīnguǎn (Yuánhuáyètiānyuánbīnguǎn)
voyage.price: Listed rates for doubles including breakfast ¥228, discounted ¥163
voyage.address: 86 Westend of North Ring Road Three (西三环北路86号 Xīsānhuánběilù)
voyage.content: Rooms with free internet, aircon and fridge. Business center, beauty salon and ticket office available. Chinese restaurant.

voyage.name: Longwu Jingpin Hotel
voyage.alt: 北京隆屋精品酒店; Běijīnglóngwūjīngpǐnjiǔdiàn
voyage.price: Listed price for doubles from ¥250, discounted from ¥198; breakfast ¥20
voyage.address: 35 Enjili (恩济里35号 ēnjìlǐ)
voyage.content: Rooms with free internet. The cheapest rooms are quite small. Business center, beauty salon, ticket office and laundry service available.

voyage.name: Beijing Zhong Yu Century Grand Hotel
voyage.alt: 北京中裕世纪大酒店 Běijīng Zhōng Yù Shìjì Dàjiǔdiàn
voyage.address: 31 Lianhuachi East Road 西客站北广场莲花池东路31号
voyage.content: Located in Haidian District, the second-largest district in the capital’s urban area. It offers 208 air-conditioned rooms and appointed with a cable TV, mini-bar, refrigerator, room safe, IDD/ DDD telephone and broadband Internet.

voyage.name: Beijing Xinyuan Hotel
voyage.price: Best rates on official website start at ¥664
voyage.address: 6 Shifangyuan St
voyage.content: Offers 361 air-conditioned guestrooms, all of which have cable TV, a hair dryer, and safe. High speed Internet access is also available. Some of its amenities include indoor swimming pool, gym and sauna, tennis court, and night club.

voyage.name: Central Garden Hotel Beijing
voyage.address: No.18, Gaoliangqiao Xie Street

voyage.name: Friendship Hotel
voyage.address: 1 Zhongguancun Nandajie 中关村南大街1号
voyage.content: Built back in 1954 for foreign visitors to Beijing, this has been extensively modernized and remains a busy hotel.

voyage.name: Royal King Hotel
voyage.alt: 融金国际酒店 Róngjīn Guójì Jiǔdiàn
voyage.address: 39 Xueyuan S Rd, Beixiaguan
voyage.content: Has convenient access to the country's so-called Silicon Valley, Zhongguancun, and many of the city's cultural and historic attractions. Their rooms are air-conditioned and fitted with free high-speed Internet access, LCD TV with satellite channels, a DDD/ IDD phone, and private toilet and bath with sprinkler shower. Among their facilities includes a health club that features steam bath, gymnasium, and jacuzzi, spa,

voyage.name: Sariz International Hotel
voyage.address: The Gate Building, 19 Zhongguancun Avenue
voyage.content: This 5-star hotel is a 15-minute drive from the Bird's Nest stadium and Water Cube. It offers 224 air-conditioned guestrooms and is equipped with an LCD TV with cable, computer, broadband Internet, mini-bar, and refrigerator. It offers top class facilities and services such as Chinese and Western Restaurants, fitness center, health club, and three meeting rooms.

voyage.name: Shanshui Trends Hotel
voyage.alt: 山水时尚酒店 (北京航天桥店); Shānshuǐshíshàngjiǔdiàn (Běijīnghángtiānqiáodiàn)
voyage.price: Listed rates for doubles from ¥388, discounted ¥181; no breakfast available.
voyage.address: 10 Fucheng Road (阜成路10号 Fùchénglù)
voyage.content: Rooms with free internet and aircon. Gift shop, ticket office and laundry service available. Chinese restaurant and rooms service.

voyage.name: Shen Zhou International Hotel
voyage.address: 31 Zhongguancun South Avenue
voyage.content: Air-conditioned accommodations, all of which have cable TV, Internet access, telephone with voicemail, and electronic safe. Some of its amenities include grm, spa and Internet café.

voyage.name: Somerset ZhongGuanCun Beijing
voyage.alt: 北京盛捷中关村服务公寓
voyage.address: No 15 Haidian Zhong St
voyage.content: Kitchen and living areas and broadband internet access.

voyage.name: Xinxing Hotel
voyage.alt: 北京新兴宾馆 Běijīng Xīnxīng Bīnguǎn
voyage.address: No.17 the 3rd Ring Rd Middle West 西三北中路17号
voyage.content: Free internet access, but you need to ask for a room with it (you should also ask in advance too). The staff are friendly, but their English is minimal. It is mostly Chinese tourists and businessmen that stay here. Chinese breakfast is served on the second floor in the morning until 09:00. There is also a swimming pool in a separate building.

voyage.name: Crowne Plaza Beijing Zhongguancun
voyage.alt: 北京中关村皇冠假日酒店; Běijīng Zhōngguāncūnhuángguānjiàrì Jiǔdiàn
voyage.price: Listed rates for doubles from ¥1,826, discounted rates from ¥772, breakfast ¥170 (included for more expensive rooms)
voyage.address: 106 Zhichun Road (知春路106号 Zhīchūnlù)
voyage.content: Rooms with internet access (against surcharge in cheaper rooms). Business center, fitness, swimming pool and sauna available. Chinese and Western restaurants as well as bar. The service is ok, but the level of English spoken here is a bit disappointing. The location is not very interesting, but the metro is not far away.

voyage.name: Diaoyutai State Guesthouse
voyage.address: 2 Fucheng Road (阜成路2号)
voyage.content: Once reserved for high-ranking foreign VIPs and officials, the guesthouse now offers service to regular travellers as well, albeit price varies.

voyage.name: China Central Television (CCTV) Headquarters
voyage.alt: 中央电视台新楼 Zhōngyāng Diànshìtái Xīnlóu
voyage.content: Just north-east of Guomao station along the Third Ring Road is this beautiful and unique tower by Dutch architects Rem Koolhaas and Ole Scheeren, housing China Central Television.

voyage.name: CITIC Tower (China Zun)
voyage.content: Beijing's tallest building (528m) completed in 2018. Its distinctive shape is inspired by the ancient Chinese zun ritual wine vessel and it dominates the CBD skyline just southeast of Guomao.

voyage.name: World Trade Center Tower III
voyage.content: Just north-west of Guomao station, this 338m skyscraper is Beijing's second tallest building. It houses offices, the China World Summit Wing hotel, and restaurants and bars with panoramic city views. The terrace at Migas Mercado offers one of the city's best nighttime views of the illuminated CCTV Headquarters.

voyage.name: World Trade Center Phase 3B
voyage.alt: 国贸三期B Guómào Sānqī B
voyage.content: Completed in 2017, this 296m tower stands immediately beside Tower III as part of the China World Trade Center complex, contributing to the iconic Guomao skyline.

voyage.name: Dongyue Temple
voyage.address: 141 Chaowai Street (朝外大街141号; Cháowàidàjiē)
voyage.content: Taoist temple founded in 1319 with hundreds of life size plaster figures and the possibility of making offerings to different gods responsible for all kind of stuff. The temple also houses the Beijing Folk Arts Museum. Very quiet and peaceful spot.

voyage.name: Xihuang Temple
voyage.address: No. 11 Huangsi Street, Chaoyang
voyage.content: A Gelugpa monastery of Tibetan Buddhism. It is the location of High-level Tibetan Buddhism College of China and the residence of the current Panchen Lama. Requires reservation 7 days early on the WeChat public account "西黄寺博物馆" at 09:00, only 300 tickets available each day.

voyage.name: Chaoyang Park
voyage.address: 1 Nongzhan South Road (农展南路1号; Nóngzhǎn Nánlù)
voyage.content: The largest park in Beijing at 3 km by 1.5 km. The park features an artificial beach, two large swimming pools, a bungee jumping tower, boat rental, concert stages, sports areas, a number of amusement park rides and flower areas. The individual entertainment options might not be impressive, but the size of the park and the number of local visitors makes a stroll here delightful anyway.

voyage.name: Ritan Park
voyage.address: 6 Ritan North Road (日坛北路6号; Rìtán Běilù)
voyage.content: The park contains the Temple of the Sun with an altar built in 1530 and used for sacrifices to the sun. Great park with entertainment for the children, good cafés and restaurants, plenty of local life to watch and also historical stuff. The altar is a round open space popular for flying kites. If you couldn't get close to the "Echo Wall" at Temple of Heaven due to crowds, you can do the same trick here (although only

voyage.name: Happy Valley Amusement Park
voyage.address: Xiaowuji North Road, Southend of East Ring Road Four (东四环南路小武基北路; Dōngsìhuánnánlù Xiǎowǔjīběilù)
voyage.content: Amusement park established in 2006 and by far the largest in Beijing covering around 1 km² and comprising more than 40 rides divided in different themed areas.

voyage.name: Honglingjin Park
voyage.address: Houbalizhuang, East Ring Road Four (东四环路后八里庄5号; Dōngsìhuánlù Hòubālǐzhuāng)
voyage.content: Here you can watch sculptures and gingko trees. The park also features indoor and outdoor playgrounds, boats for hire and a number of amusement park rides.

voyage.name: Side Park
voyage.address: 6 Fangyuan West Road (芳园西路6号; Fāngyuán Xīlù)
voyage.content: Park featuring sport activities and playgrounds.

voyage.name: Olympic Forest Park
voyage.content: The largest city park, larger than the Central Park.

voyage.name: The North Park of the Olympic Forest Park
Yuan Dadu City Wall Ruins Park
voyage.address: Intersection of Jian'an East Road and Anzhen Road (健安东路与安贞路交叉路口)
voyage.content: The ruins of the northern city wall of Khanbaliq (Dadu), the winter capital of the Yuan Dynasty.

voyage.name: China National Film Museum
voyage.content: One of the world's largest film museums, tracing the history of Chinese cinema from the late Qing dynasty to the present day. Features historic cameras, costumes, film memorabilia, reconstructed movie sets and extensive exhibits on major Chinese films and directors.

voyage.name: China Science and Technology Museum
voyage.content: China's national science museum, featuring hundreds of hands-on exhibits covering spaceflight, robotics, transportation, physics and information technology. Also contains IMAX and dome theatres and hosts regular temporary exhibitions.

voyage.name: China Archaeology Museum
voyage.content: Major national museum showcasing archaeological discoveries from across China, including prehistoric cultures, bronzes, ceramics, tomb artefacts and relics from early Chinese civilizations.

voyage.name: China National Arts & Crafts Museum
voyage.content: National museum dedicated to traditional Chinese decorative arts and intangible cultural heritage. Exhibits include jade, lacquerware, embroidery, cloisonné, textiles and masterworks of traditional craftsmanship.

voyage.name: Museum of the Communist Party of China
voyage.alt: 中国共产党历史展览馆
voyage.content: A comprehensive museum on the history of the Communist Party of China and modern Chinese history. Opened in 2021.

voyage.name: Red Sandalwood Museum
voyage.content: Founded by collector Chen Lihua, this museum houses one of the world's largest collections of traditional zitan (red sandalwood) furniture, architectural models and decorative arts.

voyage.name: China Sports Museum
voyage.content: Museum covering the history of Chinese sport and Olympic participation, with exhibits on major athletes, international competitions and the development of sport in modern China.

voyage.name: Art Museum of the Beijing Fine Art Academy
voyage.content: Museum attached to the Beijing Fine Art Academy, known for exhibitions of traditional Chinese painting, calligraphy and works by influential modern masters including Qi Baishi.

voyage.name: China Ethnic Museum
voyage.alt: 中华民族园 (中华民族博物院); Zhōnghuámínzúyuán (Zhōnghuámínzúbówùyuàn); Chinese Ethnic Culture Park; China Nationalities Museum
voyage.address: 1 Minzuyuan Road (民族园路1号; Mínzúyuánlù)
voyage.content: Large anthropological museum and cultural park showcasing the cultures of China's 56 officially recognized ethnic groups. The site combines exhibition halls with full-scale reconstructions of traditional villages, houses, temples and landscapes, along with regular cultural performances and festivals. Covers about 50 hectares in two sections (North and South Parks).

voyage.name: Ethnic Costume Museum
voyage.content: Specialized museum affiliated with the Beijing Institute of Fashion Technology, displaying traditional costumes, textiles, embroidery, jewelry and ornaments from China's many ethnic groups. Particularly strong for research on ethnic dress and textile traditions. For a broader collection of ethnic artifacts, costumes and historical exhibits, see the Cultural Palace of Nationalities (民族文化宫) near Fuxingmen in Xicheng Di

voyage.name: Museum of Tibetan Culture
voyage.content: Museum dedicated to Tibetan history, religion and culture, with exhibits on traditional art, manuscripts, architecture and daily life across the Tibetan Plateau.

voyage.name: National Museum for Modern Chinese Scientists
voyage.content: Highlights the lives and achievements of leading Chinese scientists, engineers and inventors from the late Qing period to the present day.

voyage.name: National Museum of Modern Chinese Literature
voyage.content: China's principal museum of modern literature, with exhibits on major twentieth-century writers, original manuscripts, personal belongings and reconstructed studies.

voyage.name: China Railway Museum
voyage.content: Museum devoted to the history of China's railways, featuring historic locomotives, railway equipment and exhibits on the development of the country's rail network.

voyage.name: National Stadium
voyage.alt: 北京国家体育场; Běijīng Guójiā Tǐyùchǎng
voyage.address: Olympic Park, Chaoyang District
voyage.content: Known as the "Bird’s Nest" (鸟巢), this Herzog & de Meuron-designed stadium is Beijing’s most recognisable Olympic landmark. It hosts major sporting events and concerts, and remains a primary architectural and tourism attraction.

voyage.name: National Aquatics Center
voyage.alt: 国家游泳中心; Guójiā Yóuyǒng Zhōngxīn
voyage.address: Olympic Green, Chaoyang District
voyage.content: Known as the "Water Cube" (水立方), this distinctive venue has been partially repurposed for swimming, exhibitions, and seasonal light shows.

voyage.name: National Indoor Stadium
voyage.address: Olympic Green, Chaoyang District
voyage.content: A multi-purpose arena used for ice sports, concerts, and events, remaining an active venue within the Olympic Green complex.

voyage.name: Olympic Green Tennis Center
voyage.address: Olympic Green, Chaoyang District
voyage.content: A major tennis complex that continues to host professional tournaments and public sporting events.

voyage.name: Olympic Sports Center Stadium
voyage.address: Beichen Road area
voyage.content: A renovated multi-purpose stadium used for football matches, athletics, and concerts.

voyage.name: Beijing Workers’ Stadium
voyage.address: Gongti North Road
voyage.content: A major modernised stadium and entertainment complex anchoring the Gongti district, hosting football matches, concerts, and large-scale events.

voyage.name: UCCA Center for Contemporary Art
voyage.content: China's leading contemporary art museum and the anchor institution of the 798 Art District. Hosts major exhibitions of Chinese and international artists, along with film screenings, talks and educational programmes.

voyage.name: Tang Contemporary Art
voyage.content: One of Asia's most prominent commercial contemporary art galleries, exhibiting established and emerging Chinese and international artists.

voyage.name: Beijing Commune
voyage.content: Influential gallery representing many of China's leading contemporary artists, with exhibitions often focused on experimental and conceptually driven work.

voyage.name: Three Shadows Photography Art Centre
voyage.address: 155 Caochangdi
voyage.content: One of China's leading photography institutions, hosting exhibitions, festivals, educational programmes, a library and artist facilities.

voyage.name: Galerie Urs Meile
voyage.address: 104 Caochangdi
voyage.content: Established Swiss gallery exhibiting both Chinese and international contemporary artists.

voyage.name: China Art Archives and Warehouse
voyage.content: Influential non-profit contemporary art institution focusing on experimental Chinese art, research and archival work.

voyage.name: Century Theater
voyage.address: 40 Liangmaqiao Road (亮马桥路40号; Liàngmǎqiáolù)
voyage.content: A long-running performance venue in the Liangmaqiao/Lufthansa Centre area hosting a mix of concerts, theatre, dance, and touring productions. While once especially popular with the expat community, it now serves a broader mainstream audience and continues to operate as a multi-purpose cultural venue.

voyage.name: Chaoyang Theater
voyage.hours: Performances typically in the late afternoon and evening
voyage.address: 36 North East Third Ring Road (东三环北路36号; Dōngsānhuán Běilù)
voyage.content: One of Beijing’s best-known venues for acrobatics shows, presenting highly polished, tourist-oriented performances with occasional cultural programming such as Peking opera. It remains a staple evening entertainment option in Chaoyang.

voyage.name: China Puppet Theater
voyage.alt: 中国木偶剧院; Zhōngguó Mù’ǒu Jùyuàn
voyage.address: 1 Anhua Xili, East Third Ring Road (东三环安华西里甲1号; Dōngsānhuán Ānhuáxīlǐ)
voyage.content: A dedicated theatre for puppet performances, primarily aimed at children and families. It stages both traditional Chinese stories and adapted Western classics, along with interactive educational shows.

voyage.name: Tuanjiehu Swimming Pool
voyage.alt: 团结湖游泳池; Tuánjiéhú Yóuyǒngchí
voyage.address: 16 Tuanjiehu South Road (团结湖南路16号; Tuánjiéhú Nánlù)
voyage.content: A public swimming complex that operates mainly during the summer months. Facilities typically include indoor/outdoor pools depending on the season and weather conditions. It is a straightforward municipal option rather than a leisure resort-style water park.

voyage.name: Silk Street (Xiushui Street Market)
voyage.address: 8 East Xiushui St., Jianguomenwai Dajie
voyage.content: Once Beijing’s iconic bargaining bazaar for tourists seeking imitation luxury goods, Silk Street has been fully modernized into an air-conditioned retail complex. Today it functions more as a fixed-price or lightly negotiable mall rather than a true bargaining market.

voyage.name: Taikoo Li Sanlitun (Sanlitun Village)
voyage.address: Corner of Gongti Beilu and Sanlitun Lu
voyage.content: An open-air, high-end retail and lifestyle district completed in phases from 2008 onward, now one of Beijing’s main international shopping and leisure hubs. It combines flagship luxury stores, global fashion brands, cafés, restaurants, and entertainment venues in a pedestrian-oriented layout. Unlike traditional malls, it is structured as a low-rise complex of interconnected blocks. It is especially busy in the evenin

voyage.name: China World Trade Center Mall (Guomao)
voyage.address: 1 Jianguomenwai Dajie
voyage.content: A large high-end shopping complex integrated into Beijing’s central business district skyline. The mall is dominated by luxury and premium international brands, business-oriented retail, and upscale dining. It caters primarily to office workers and affluent shoppers rather than tourists, with pricing and positioning firmly at the premium end of the market.

voyage.name: Panjiayuan Antique Market
voyage.address: 29 Tianya Hongqiao Rd, Chaoyang
voyage.content: Beijing’s largest flea and antique market, now operating largely as a curated mix of antiques, replicas, collectibles, and cultural crafts. While genuine antiques exist, the majority of goods are modern reproductions or decorative items. The market remains popular for browsing and souvenir hunting rather than serious antiquities trading. Bargaining is still expected, especially for higher-priced stalls, but pricing h

voyage.name: Guwan Cheng Antique Market (Ancient Arts City)
voyage.address: North of Panjiayuan, East 3rd Ring Road
voyage.content: A multi-storey indoor antique and collectibles complex positioned slightly upmarket from Panjiayuan. It focuses on ceramics, furniture, calligraphy, and curated “antique-style” pieces. Compared with Panjiayuan’s outdoor flea-market atmosphere, Guwan Cheng is more formal, with greater emphasis on established dealers and higher entry pricing. As always in Beijing’s antiques trade, authenticity varies and buyer caution

voyage.name: Friendship Store (Jianguomen Branch)
voyage.address: CITIC Building, Jianguomenwai Dajie
voyage.content: A legacy department store from the early reform era when foreign visitors had restricted retail access. Today it operates as a quiet, fixed-price retail space with mid- to high-end goods. It is no longer a practical shopping destination for value, but remains of historical interest as a symbol of earlier foreign-access retail in Beijing.

voyage.name: Liangma Flower Market
voyage.address: Behind Kempinski Hotel, Lufthansa Centre area
voyage.content: A large indoor flower and home goods market. The ground floor focuses on cut flowers and plants at low prices, while upper levels sell kitchenware, decorative items, and household goods. It remains one of the better-value casual shopping options in the Lufthansa embassy district.

voyage.name: The Place (Shimao Tianjie)
voyage.address: 9 Guanghua Lu / 光华路9号
voyage.content: An outdoor commercial complex best known for its massive overhead LED canopy screen, which displays synchronized light shows in the evening. Beyond the visual attraction, it contains mid-range retail shops, cafés, and restaurants.

voyage.name: Side Street Jianguomen
voyage.content: Popular local burger place owned by Indian expat, known for creative burgers and strong value. Widely regarded as one of Beijing’s better casual burger options.

voyage.name: Khan Baba
voyage.content: Long-running Pakistani restaurant popular with diplomats, expats and students. Serves kebabs, curries, biryani, naan and other South Asian and Middle Eastern dishes. Service can be slow at peak times.

voyage.name: The Middle 8th
voyage.content: Well-known Yunnan restaurant featuring mushroom dishes, grilled fish and regional specialties.

voyage.name: Mosto
voyage.content: Modern Mediterranean restaurant with a large terrace and extensive wine list.

voyage.name: Home Plate BBQ
voyage.content: Texas-style barbecue and one of Beijing’s long-established expat dining institutions.

voyage.name: Turkish Feast
voyage.content: Turkish restaurant serving kebabs, pide, mezze and desserts.

voyage.name: Migas Mercado
voyage.address: China World Mall
voyage.content: Spanish tapas and paella restaurant with floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking the Beijing CBD skyline, including close views of the CCTV Headquarters.

voyage.name: Hua's Restaurant
voyage.address: Various branches
voyage.content: Upscale Beijing cuisine and seafood served in traditional courtyard-style settings.

voyage.name: Xi He Ya Yuan
voyage.address: Ritan area
voyage.content: Well-known restaurant specializing in Peking duck and refined northern Chinese cuisine.

voyage.name: Makye Ame
voyage.address: Jianguomenwai area
voyage.content: Tibetan restaurant with traditional décor and occasional cultural performances.

voyage.name: Opera Bombana
voyage.address: Parkview Green Fangcaodi (芳草地)
voyage.content: Elegant Italian fine dining by chef Umberto Bombana, known for refined tasting menus and high-quality ingredients. One of Beijing’s top upscale Italian restaurants.

voyage.name: Da Dong
voyage.address: Tuanjiehu and other branches
voyage.content: One of Beijing’s most famous Peking duck restaurants. Reservations recommended.

voyage.name: TRB Hutong
voyage.address: Shatan North Street
voyage.content: Fine dining in a restored historic building near the Forbidden City. Frequently ranked among Beijing’s top special-occasion restaurants.

voyage.name: Bottega
voyage.address: Taikoo Li Sanlitun
voyage.content: Upscale Italian restaurant popular with expats and business diners.

voyage.name: The Kunlun Beijing
voyage.address: 2 Xinyuan South Road
voyage.content: Large traditional 5-star hotel. The 29th-floor revolving restaurant offers panoramic views of the skyline of the CDB as the dining floor slowly rotates. Coffee in the afternoon costs 78 RMB including service. There is also a huge Moutai shop in the lobby, with Moutai bottles in all sizes.

voyage.name: Grand Millennium Beijing
voyage.address: Dongsanhuan Middle Road, CBD
voyage.content: Large-scale 5-star business hotel in central Chaoyang CBD corridor.

voyage.name: Hotel Jen Beijing
voyage.address: China World Trade Center Tower B, CBD
voyage.content: Contemporary 5-star business and lifestyle hotel occupying China World Tower Phase 3B. A stylish and generally better-value alternative to the more expensive China World Summit Wing in the neighboring tower.

voyage.name: China World Summit Wing, Beijing
voyage.address: China World Tower, China World Trade Center, CBD
voyage.content: Ultra-luxury Shangri-La hotel occupying the upper floors of China World Tower Phase 3A, Beijing's iconic 330-meter CBD skyscraper. The hotel offers panoramic city views and an unusually vertical hotel experience, with guest rooms beginning on the 64th floor.

voyage.name: Rosewood Beijing
voyage.content: Widely regarded as one of Beijing's finest luxury hotels, featuring spacious rooms, Michelin-starred dim sum, and one of the city's strongest luxury breakfast buffets, including eggs Benedict made to order at the egg station. The property is also known for its sophisticated design and the stylish Mei Bar.

voyage.name: Park Hyatt Beijing
voyage.address: Beijing Yintai Centre
voyage.content: High-rise luxury hotel occupying the upper floors of Beijing Yintai Centre, known for sweeping skyline views.

voyage.name: Four Seasons Hotel Beijing
voyage.address: 48 Liangmaqiao Road
voyage.content: Contemporary luxury hotel in the embassy district, known for extensive wellness facilities and one of Beijing's most impressive indoor pools.

voyage.name: Bvlgari Hotel Beijing
voyage.address: Building 2, Genesis Beijing, Xinyuan South Road
voyage.content: Exclusive Italian luxury hotel featuring elegant contemporary interiors

voyage.name: Hotel Éclat Beijing
voyage.address: Parkview Green FangCaoDi, Dongdaqiao Road
voyage.content: Boutique luxury hotel distinguished by its extensive contemporary art collection

voyage.name: CHAO Sanlitun Beijing
voyage.address: No. 4 Gongti East Road, Chaoyang District
voyage.content: Design-focused lifestyle hotel combining luxury accommodation with galleries, cultural programming and a private club atmosphere.

voyage.name: Outer Court
voyage.content: The imposing set of buildings designed to be the ceremonial centre of the palace. Visitors enter through Meridian Gate (A), the imposing main gate with unique protruding side wings, followed by the Gate of Supreme Harmony (F), where the Emperor sometimes held court. There are then three grand halls set on a multi-tiered marble platform, including the Hall of Supreme Harmony (G), which was the ceremonial throne room u

voyage.name: Paintings and Calligraphy Gallery - Hall of Military Eminence
voyage.content: Somewhat ironically, this set of buildings (H) built to celebrate military valour now houses the Palace Museum's paintings and calligraphy gallery. Works from the Palace Museum's extensive collection are rotated through the gallery and changed every few months. To reach the Hall of Military Eminence, go through the gate on the left after the Meridian Gate but before going through the Gate of Supreme Harmony.

voyage.name: Porcelain and Ceramics - Hall of Literary Glory
voyage.content: This mini-palace (J) was variously used as the Crown Prince's court and an imperial Confucian lecture hall. It now houses the Palace Museum's porcelain and ceramics gallery. The gallery's exhibits trace through the development of Chinese porcelain, and includes items from the large imperial collection held by the Palace Museum. To reach the Hall of Literary Glory, go through the gate on the right after the Meridian G

voyage.name: Inner Palace
voyage.content: Form the Outer Court, the central section of the Inner Palace is accessed through the Gate of Heavenly Purity. The Inner Palace, like the Outer Court, is centred on three main buildings. The grandest, the Palace of Heavenly Purity (L) was designed to house the Emperor's bed chamber, but later became a throne room where the Emperor held court with his ministers. The Palace of Earthly Tranquillity was designed to be th

voyage.name: Treasures Gallery - Palace of Tranquil Longevity
voyage.content: A palace in itself with its own "Outer Court", "Inner Palace" and "Imperial Garden", this complex (O) was designed for the Qianlong Emperor to enjoy his retirement after abdication - but he was too busy giving his son instructions on government to ever use it. Look for the glaze-tiled Nine Dragon Screen in front of the main entrance. These buildings now house the Palace Museum's Treasures Gallery (珍宝馆), which include

voyage.name: Clocks Gallery - Hall of Ancestral Offerings
voyage.content: Built as a shrine for making offerings to ancestors, this set of buildings on the eastern side of the Inner Palace now houses the Palace Museum's clocks display, the major portion of which are elaborate European-style mechanical clocks - including a calligraphy-writing automaton! Demonstrations are held at 11:00 and 14:00, where some of the fanciest clocks in the collections are put on show. Separate admission charge

voyage.name: Imperial Garden
voyage.content: The Palace's main garden is among the smallest of Beijing's imperial gardens, but the emperors have managed to pack a lot of pavilions, ponds, trees and ornamental rocks into the space. It would be a nice place to relax after your tour of the Forbidden City, if it weren't packed with thousands of tourists with exactly the same idea. The Imperial Garden leads in the north to the Gate of Divine Might, the north gate an

voyage.name: Wall, moat and corner towers
voyage.content: The Forbidden City's imposing walls and tranquil moat can only be admired from outside the complex. As you leave the Forbidden City, the corner towers (E) are well worth seeing for their elaborate roof structure, modelled on mythical "ideal" pavilions in Chinese art.

voyage.name: Imperial Ancestral Temple
voyage.content: This is one of the grandest temple complexes in Beijing, often forgotten by visitors keen to get to or from the nearby Forbidden City. The temple complex is located to the east of the ceremonial way leading from Tiananmen Square to Meridian Gate. This was where the Emperor performed rites to honour his own ancestors. Sadly, much of the interior, including the ancestral tablets, were destroyed by Red Guards during the

voyage.name: Altar of Land and Grain
voyage.price: ¥3 (park); ¥5 (inner gardens); seasonal prices apply during flowering season
voyage.content: Located west of the ceremonial way leading from Tiananmen Square to Meridian Gate in a mirrored position to the Imperial Ancestral Temple, the Emperor came to this altar to venerate the land of his empire, rather than his family. The park surrounding the temple is called Zhongshan Park. There are fewer grand buildings here, but the gardens and greenhouses are famed for their flowers, which are on show year-round.

voyage.name: Upright Gate
voyage.content: The Upright Gate is located between Tiananmen gate and the Meridian Gate, along the ceremonial way. It is nearly identical to Tiananmen gate, and is also open to the public.

voyage.name: Shopping
voyage.content: Souvenir stores and stalls of varying quality dot the Forbidden City. Many of these are overpriced tourist traps, but if you are interested in Chinese art, it can be a good place to find the Palace Museum's high-quality reproductions of paintings and other artworks from its collection.

voyage.name: Clocks demonstration
voyage.address: Clocks gallery - Hall of Ancestral Offering
voyage.content: Some of the fanciest mechanical clocks from the Imperial collection are wound up and put into action twice a day - watch them reveal their elaborate surprises.

voyage.name: Lai Jin Yu Xuan
voyage.content: This 100-year-old restaurant is located within Zhongshan Park, just outside the Forbidden City's walls to the south west. It was a favourite haunt of Beijing's literati in the 20th century, and is today famed for its "Red Mansion" banquet, with dishes taken from the classical Chinese novel Dreams of the Red Chamber. The Lai Jin Yu Xuan tea house is also in the same park, and is a good place to enjoy a cup of tea amid

voyage.name: Cheng Fu Yan
voyage.address: 38 Nanchangjie
voyage.content: One of Beijing's famed "imperial cuisine" restaurants that also has a private dining room decorated as a replica of Chairman Mao's study, Cheng Fu Yan's odd combination of the imperial and revolutionary reflects its location - just outside the Forbidden City's south wall and faces the leadership compound of Zhongnanhai across the street. The owner's grandfather spent 22 years cooking for Chairman Mao and Madame Mao.

voyage.name: Forbidden City Cafe
voyage.content: After the controversial Forbidden City branch of Starbucks closed in 2007, the former Duty Room of the Nine Ministers has hosted a very similar café run by the Palace Museum. The prices are high but comparable to Starbucks prices in China, and the selection of drinks and snacks is also similar.

voyage.name: Lai Jin Yu Xuan Teahouse
voyage.address: Inside Zhongshan Park
voyage.content: Associated with Lai Jin Yu Xuan Restaurant (see "Eat" listing above), this is a peaceful tea house within Zhongshan Park set amongst mature cypress trees, in the south west of the Forbidden City precinct outside the Forbidden City walls.

voyage.name: Chairman Mao Memorial Hall
voyage.hours: Tue-Sun 08:00-12:00 (but it is sometimes closed without notice)
voyage.content: The body of the founder of the People's Republic of China, Mao Zedong, has been preserved (against his own wishes) and is on display in here. Expect huge, but moving, queues. No bags, cameras or water bottles are allowed inside and must be dropped off (for a fee) at the bag-check building across the road to the east (mobile phones are permitted). Flowers can be purchased to lay at the feet of Mao's statue inside (alt

voyage.name: Monument to the People's Heroes
voyage.content: A cenotaph with round-the-clock honor guard commemorating the PRC's veterans and war dead. Illuminated at night. Usually blocked off unless there is an important ceremony or visitors, but even then only those participating can go to the base of the cenotaph. However, you can usually get close enough to take pictures.

voyage.name: Great Hall of the People
voyage.content: The seat of the National People's Congress (NPC), China's unicameral legislature, as well as the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC), its main political advisory body. Both assemblies convene here once a year for about ten days in what is known as the "Two Sessions" (两会). Meetings of both assemblies take place in the Great Auditorium, with their times staggered to avoid conflicts. In addition t

voyage.name: Tian'anmen Gate
voyage.alt: 天安门; Gate of Heavenly Peace
voyage.content: Tian'anmen Gate, and its large portrait of Chairman Mao, dominates the northern end of the square. This was originally the main gate into the Imperial City, and is the only one of the four gates that still survives. Pass beneath the gate to head north toward the Forbidden City. It costs nothing to pass through, but on the far side there is a ticket booth where you can pay admission to visit the gate. Although visitin

voyage.name: Zhongshan Park
voyage.address: West side of Tian'anmen (天安门西侧; Tiānānménxīcè)
voyage.content: Beautifully landscaped park with lots of trees and bamboo. The Forbidden City, covered in a separate article, is entered through this park. Paddle boats for rent on the moat of the Forbidden City. Also an indoor playground for children, and bumper cars.

voyage.name: Zhengyangmen
voyage.content: Built in 1419 as the front gate of the inner city wall. It was only used by the emperor on his way to Tiantan. Now it houses exhibits with photos and models of the old city.

voyage.name: Zhihua Temple
voyage.alt: 智化寺; Zhìhuàsì; also known as Temple of Wisdom Attained
voyage.address: 5 Lumicang Hutong (禄米仓胡同5号; Lùmǐcānghútòng)
voyage.content: Buddhist temple built in 1443. One of the largest, oldest and best preserved wooden structures in Beijing. Houses the Ancient Music Center, which now and then gives concerts according to ancient traditions at 10:00 and 15:00. Also houses the Beijing Cultural Exchange Museum. It has been renovated. Free tour guide at 09:30 and 14:00.

voyage.name: Imperial Ancestral Temple
voyage.price: ¥2, does not include entry into buildings
voyage.content: This was the temple where the emperors and other members of the royal family would pay respect to their ancestors. The buildings are original, though much of the interior, including the ancestral tablets, were destroyed during the Cultural Revolution. It has since been repurposed as a museum dedicated to the working class Chinese.

voyage.name: Beijing Police Museum
voyage.alt: 北京警察博物馆; Běijīng Jǐngchá Bówùguǎn
voyage.hours: 09:00-16:00, no entry after 15:30, closed on Mondays
voyage.address: 36 Dongjiaomin Lane (东交民巷36号; Dōngjiāomín Xiàng)
voyage.content: Large museum on police history.

voyage.name: China Court Museum
voyage.alt: 中国法院博物馆; Zhōngguó Fǎyuàn Bówùguǎn
voyage.hours: 09:00-17:00, no entry after 16:00, closed on Mondays
voyage.address: 4 Zhengyi Road (正义路4号; Zhèngyì Lù)
voyage.content: A museum about the court system in China. The museum is in a historic building dating from 1910 that was originally the Beijing branch of the Yokohama Specie Bank, a Japanese bank.

voyage.name: China Customs Museum
voyage.alt: 中国海关博物馆; Zhōngguó Hǎiguān Bówùguǎn
voyage.hours: 09:00-16:30, no tickets issued after 15:45, no entry permitted after 16:00, closed on Mondays
voyage.address: 2 Jianguomen Inner Avenue (建国门内大街2号; Jiànguómén Nèi Dàjiē
voyage.content: A national-level museum run by the General Administration of Customs of the People's Republic of China.

voyage.name: China National Museum of Women and Children
voyage.alt: 中国妇女儿童博物馆; Zhōngguó Fùnǚ Értóng Bówùguǎn, Museum of Chinese Women and Children
voyage.address: 9 Beijige Road (北极阁路9号; Běijígé Lù
voyage.content: A museum exhibiting numerous cultural and historical artefacts related to women and children in China. Visitors are expected to make a booking on WeChat at least one day before visiting the museum. The museum's WeChat account may be found by searching "中国妇女儿童博物馆公众号".

voyage.name: Imperial City Art Museum
voyage.address: 9 Changpuheyan (菖蒲河沿9号; Chāngpúhéyàn)
voyage.content: The Imperial City was the Manchu city that surrounded the Forbidden City during the Qing dynasty. The museum's centrepiece is a scale model of the Forbidden & Imperial Cities. There are also displays on lifestyle, costumes, arts & crafts of the Qing imperial city. Occasionally hosts special exhibits that cost extra.

voyage.name: National Museum of China
voyage.alt: 中国国家博物馆 Zhōngguó Guójiā Bówùguǎn
voyage.price: Free; foreign visitors must show their passport
voyage.address: 16 East Chang'an St, (东长安街16马 Dōngcháng'ānjiē)
voyage.content: A huge museum containing the ancient and recent history of the Chinese nation. Modern history exhibit focuses on the successes of the Communist Party (and obviously not the negatives). Most exhibits have short English explanations.

voyage.name: Shijia Hutong Museum
voyage.alt: 史家胡同博物馆; Shíjiā Hútóng Bówùguǎn
voyage.address: 24 Shijia Hutong (史家胡同24号; Shíjiā Hútóng
voyage.content: A traditional courtyard residence that has been turned into a museum. There are exhibitions about the history of the hutong and the daily lives of the residents.

voyage.name: CourtYard Gallery
voyage.address: 53 Donganmen Dajie (东安门大街53号; Dōngānméndàjiē)
voyage.content: Founded in 1996. Exhibits emerging and mid-career artists working in a wide range of media.

voyage.name: Wan Fung Art Gallery
voyage.address: 136 Nanchizi Jie
voyage.content: Worth a peek if you're in the area. Housed in a side building in the courtyard of the Imperial Archives, which you can't go in, but is quite impressive. The courtyard itself is a quiet corner in an otherwise crowded area of the city.

voyage.name: Legation Quarter
voyage.content: The legation quarter was once, as its name suggests, home to Beijing's many foreign diplomatic missions. During the 1900 Boxer Rebellion, the diplomats and Chinese Christians who sought their protection held out here until a 55-day siege was broken by foreign forces coming over the city walls. The embassies have since moved to larger quarters elsewhere, but the buildings remain. Now occupied by various Chinese govern

voyage.name: Ancient Observatory
voyage.address: 2 Dongbiaobei Hutong (东裱褙胡同2号; Dōngbiǎobèihútòng)
voyage.content: The observatory, built in 1442, has been open to the public since 1983. Ancient star maps and instruments to watch stars can be seen here. Displays on the history of Chinese astronomy, and several large astronomical instruments set on top of an old watchtower of the city walls.

voyage.name: Chaonei No. 81
voyage.address: 81 Chaoyangmen Inner St, 朝阳门街道内81号
voyage.content: This abandoned, overgrown Baroque Revival complex, dating to the early 20th century, has acquired an international reputation as the best-known allegedly haunted house in China. According to residents of the nearby hutongs, even the Red Guards moved out after a few days, supposedly scared off by the ghost of a Kuomintang officer's mistress who hanged herself when he fled to Taiwan without her. It inspired the 2014 fi

voyage.name: Changpu River Park
voyage.content: Narrow strip of landscaped park along a small stream. Begins in the east near the Beijing hotel and runs almost to Tian'anmen Gate.

voyage.name: Capital Theater
voyage.address: 22 Wangfujing Street (王府井大街22号; Wángfǔjǐngdàjiē)
voyage.content: This theater is used by different theater groups, including Beijing People's Art Theater. Performances include both contemporary and classical Chinese plays.

voyage.name: Chang'an Grand Theater
voyage.address: 7 Jianguomennei Street (建国门内大街7号; Jiànguóménnèidàjiē)
voyage.content: Traditional Chinese performances with focus on Beijing Opera. Also has a shop with paintings and folk handicrafts.

voyage.name: China Children's Art Theater
voyage.address: 64 Donganmen Street (东安门大街64号; Dōngānméndàjiē)
voyage.content: Established in 1956. Stages children's plays.

voyage.name: Dongyuan Theater
voyage.address: Inside the Garden of Changpu River (菖蒲河公园内; Chāngpúhégōngyuánnèi)

voyage.name: Goldsail Concert Hall
voyage.address: 24 Wangfujing Street (24 Wangfujing Street (王府井大街24号; Wángfǔjǐngdàjiē)
voyage.content: Small concert hall without speakers. Suitable for chamber music also.

voyage.name: Hutong Cuisine Cooking School
voyage.address: 35 Dengcao Hutong (灯草胡同35号)
voyage.content: A few places around Nanluoguxiang now offer Chinese cooking classes. One such place, Hutong Cuisine, is run by an English-speaking chef in a small hutong home. Classes are small. Reservations are necessary. Optional market tours are also conducted before cooking classes commence.

voyage.name: New China Children's Store
voyage.alt: 新中国儿童用品商店; Xīnzhōngguóértóngyòngpǐnshāngdiàn
voyage.address: 168 Wangfujing Street (王府井大街168号; Wángfǔjǐngdàjiē)
voyage.content: Play center for children where the kids can catch goldfish, play in the gigantic sandpit or other. They also sell all kind of gear for children.

voyage.name: Wangfujing
voyage.content: Beijing's most famous shopping street, nowadays with mostly the same international brands and modern malls you will find anywhere else in the world. The street is pedestrianised for several blocks, making it pleasant to walk around. Several large malls in the area such as Oriental Plaza (see below) and Sun Dong An plaza. One useful shop is the Foreign Language Bookstore, at the northern end of the pedestrian area, wh

voyage.name: The Malls at Oriental Plaza
voyage.alt: 东方新天地 Dōngfāng Xīn Tiāndì
voyage.address: East of Tian'anmen Square, on Wangfujing
voyage.content: At one time this was the largest mall in Asia. Modern shopping mall is expensive but provides you with a lot of buying opportunities from diamonds, to real (affordable) DVDs, (international) music CDs and food. You can find lots of brands in Oriental Plaza, from high-end to low. Besides shopping, you also can eat here, from Western cuisine to traditional Chinese food.

voyage.name: Poetry Cafe
voyage.address: No 15 Nanchizi street Dongcheng District Beijing (南池子大街15号故宫东华门旁
voyage.content: A beautiful cafe with soul as its name "Poetry", is operated by a lovely young lady, who enjoys travel and photography, that she gathers a group of 'specialists' in those fields; thus, customers can get tonnes of information about travel and photography. Customers can enjoy a view of the Forbidden City over a perfectly brewed coffee.

voyage.name: Wangfujing Snack Street
voyage.content: Many stalls selling Beijing-style snacks, both sweet and savoury.

voyage.name: Donghuamen Night Market
voyage.content: The place to come for exotic snacks such as scorpions, starfish, and silkworm grubs. You can also buy more typical snacks like fried noodles, dumplings, and kebabs. More expensive than a "real" neighbourhood market, but still reasonably priced.

voyage.name: Oriental Dumpling King
voyage.address: 14 Chaoyangmen Nanxiaojie (朝阳门南小街14号楼; Cháoyángménnánxiǎojiē)
voyage.content: Cheap and delicious Dongbei (northeast) style dumplings. This is a chain, one of several around town. Their location in Harbin is recommended in several guidebooks, but if you're not going there you can get the same dumplings in Beijing. A few dozen different kinds, and can be boiled or fried. As with many dumpling places, order by weight: An order is usually two liang (èr liǎng) which is 100g, about 10-12 dumplings.

voyage.name: Donglaishun
voyage.address: 198 Wangfujing, Dong Dan,
voyage.content: This king of Beijing hotpot has been around since 1903. Founded by the Hui (ethnic Muslims), Donglaishun serves halal cuts of top-quality lamb and beef. Also serves cooked-by-chef dishes, including traditional Beijing sweets.

voyage.name: Wangfujing branch
voyage.address: 198 Wangfujing, Dajie (东城区王府井大街198号)
voyage.content: Subway: Line 1 to Wangfujing

voyage.name: Yuxin Sichuan Restaurant
voyage.content: One of the contenders in the ongoing competition for Beijing's best Sichuanese, Yuxin delivers on authenticity, flavor, and service. It's always busy, and always good.

voyage.name: Peking Chamber (Forbidden City branch)
voyage.alt: 四季民福烤鸭店（故宫店）Sìjìmínfú Kăoyā Diàn Gùgōng Diàn
voyage.address: 11 Nanchizi Dajie
voyage.content: A Peking roast duck restaurant featuring a view of the Forbidden City. Reservations suggested.

voyage.name: Dadong Duck Restaurant
voyage.alt: 大董烤鸭店 Dàdŏng Kăoyā Diàn
voyage.price: sea cucumber ¥200-600, lobster from ¥200, +10% service charge
voyage.address: Three locations in Dongcheng district
voyage.content: Considered by some to be the best Peking duck in the city, this upscale restaurant also delivers on a nice atmosphere. Reservations suggested. full/half Peking duck is ¥240/120 with extra ¥8 for condiments. Meal is served with free hot water, small soup, light fruits and black sesame for dessert.

voyage.name: Earl Bar
voyage.address: 1 Dongdan North Street (东单北大街1号; Dōngdānběidàjiē)
voyage.content: Very basic bar with local DJs.

voyage.name: Beijing City Central Youth Hostel
voyage.price: Dorms ¥60 (4-8 beds), doubles with shared bathrooms ¥160
voyage.address: 1-5 Beijing Station West St. (北京站西街1-5号; Běijīngzhàn xījiē
voyage.content: The largest hostel in Beijing, with central air conditioning and individual controls in each of the 200 rooms. It offers a computer/internet room, billiards, bar, and karaoke. On the 1st and 2nd levels are a 24-hour supermarket, breakfast bar, coffee lounge, ATM, phones for international dialing, express film processing, a mobile phone shop, and post office. The rooms on the 3rd to 6th floors include ensuites, double

voyage.name: Beijing Saga International Youth Hostel
voyage.alt: 北京实佳国际青年旅舍; Běijīng Shíjiā Guójìqīngniánlǚshè
voyage.address: 9 Shijia Hutong, Nanxiao Street (南小街史家胡同9号; Nánxiǎojiē Shǐjiāhútòng)
voyage.content: Very popular with backpackers. There's a restaurant on the top floor. The staff speak some English.

voyage.name: Eastern Morning Youth Hostel
voyage.price: Private rooms cost about ¥90 per night—book in advance
voyage.address: Dongdan Santiao, behind the Oriental Plaza
voyage.content: A great budget option if price is your primary concern. The staff do not speak much English but are friendly. Internet access is available at ¥10 per hour. It is a 5-minute walk to the Dongdan or Wangfujing subway stations and about a 15-minute walk to the International Hotel airport shuttle stop.

voyage.name: Purple Courtyard
voyage.price: Price example, ¥408 for a triple room
voyage.address: no.24 Shajing Hutong, NanLuoGuXiang, Dongcheng
voyage.content: Wonderful location in a hutong, surrounded by a mass of eateries and a couple of mini-markets. Five-minute walk to buses and Shichahai metro, 10-minute walk to Nanluoguxiang metro. Bustling area but a five-minute walk from a complex of lakes. Friendly English-speaking staff who are always available to help. TV in Chinese, free Wi-Fi, private facilities, A/C and use of fridge freezer, which is important in the Beijing

voyage.name: Wangfujing Dawan Hotel
voyage.alt: 北京王府井大万酒店; Běijīngwángfǔjǐngdàwànjiǔdiàn
voyage.price: Listed rates for doubles from ¥238, discounted from ¥137; breakfast ¥15
voyage.address: 2 Ganyu Hutong, Dongdan Bei Street (东单北大街甘雨胡同甲2号; Dōngdānběidàjiēgānyǔhútòng)
voyage.content: Rooms with free Internet, television, a/c and fridge. Business center and bath center including sauna available. Chinese restaurant. The rooms are alright, the bathrooms not too bright or clean, and the service level fluctuates, but the low price and great location make up for it.

voyage.name: Beijing Fuhao Hotel
voyage.price: Rates for doubles on official website from ¥364.47
voyage.address: 45 Wangfujing Avenue (王府井大街45号; Wáng fǔ jǐngdà jiē)
voyage.content: The hotel offers 104 air-conditioned rooms with mini-bar, cable TV, free internet and fridge. Among its facilities are Lao Chongqing Hot-pot City Restaurant, Wangfujing Roast Duck Restaurant, a sauna club, and a night club/KTV.

voyage.name: Beijing Golden Palace Silver Street
voyage.alt: 北京金府银街大酒店; Běijīngjīnfǔyínjiēdàjiǔdiàn
voyage.price: Listed rates for doubles without window from ¥588, discounted from ¥172, rooms with window somewhat more expensive; western breakfast ¥20
voyage.address: 31 Ganyu Hutong, Wangfujing Street (王府井大街甘雨胡同31号; Wángfǔjǐngdàjiē Gānyǔhútòng
voyage.content: Rooms with internet access against surcharge as well as aircon, mini bar and safe. Cheapest rooms and bathrooms are quite small and not too clean. Business center, karaoke, beauty salon, gym and rooftop garden available. Chinese and Western restaurant and a coffee shop.

voyage.name: Beijing Harmony Hotel
voyage.address: 59 Suzhou Hutong, Youtong Street
voyage.content: International 3-star hotel with 3 minutes walk to the Beijing Railway Station and Dongdan Shopping street. Convenient location for tourists.

voyage.name: Dongjiao Minxiang Hotel
voyage.address: 23A Dongjiao Minxiang, 北京东城区东交民巷甲23号
voyage.content: Offers rooms with private toilet and bath with tub, slippers, bathrobe, and hair dryer.

voyage.name: The Emperor Beijing Forbidden City Hotel
voyage.alt: 北京故宫皇家驿栈酒店, Beijing gùgōnghuángjiā yìzhàn jiǔdiàn
voyage.address: 33 Qihelou St. 东城区骑河楼大街33号
voyage.content: Boutique hotel in residential neighborhood near Forbidden City. Interestingly designed rooms are named after emperors rather than numbered. Free breakfast from rooftop restaurant with sweeping views over the Forbidden City. Long walk to subway stations.

voyage.name: Wancheng Hua Fu International Hotel
voyage.alt: 北京万程华府国际酒店
voyage.price: ¥338 for a single room. Breakfast buffet available for ¥20
voyage.address: 53 Donganmen Street, 北京东城区东安门大街53号
voyage.content: Rather basic rooms, but clean with nice bathroom and TV (Chinese channels). Some staff had trouble speaking English but all were friendly. Excellent location close to Wangfujing shopping area, 10 min walk to Forbidden City.

voyage.name: Jingyuan Courtyard Hotel - Beijing
voyage.address: 35 Xitangzi Hutong, Wangfujing Street
voyage.content: Rooms are air-conditioned and fitted with a full bath, mini-bar, cable TV, and Internet access.

voyage.name: Tangyue Hotel
voyage.price: Listed rates for doubles from ¥580, discounted from ¥207; western breakfast ¥25
voyage.address: 54 Donghuamen Road (东华门大街54号; Dōnghuàméndàjiē)
voyage.content: Spacious rooms with free internet, fridge, safe and coffee facilities. Specially designed hotel with business center, beauty salon, ticket office available. Coffee shop with first-class coffee, bar and tea house but no restaurant.

voyage.name: Beijing Hotel Nuo
voyage.alt: 北京饭店诺金; Běijīng Fàndiàn Nuòjīn
voyage.address: 33 East Chang'an Ave. (东长安街33号, Dōngcháng'ānjiē)
voyage.content: Housed in the historic French-built Block B of the former Grand Hôtel de Pékin that was completed in 1917, and the newer and more modern Block E that was completed in 2001, this is the oldest hotel in Beijing. The 1917 building is in a beautiful French Beaux-Arts architectural style.

voyage.name: Grand Hotel Beijing
voyage.alt: 北京贵宾楼饭店; Běijīng Guìbīnlóu Fàndiàn
voyage.price: Listed rates for doubles ¥3,450-14,950, discounted rates ¥765-10,500, breakfast ¥184
voyage.address: 35 East Chang'an Street (东长安街35号; Dōngchángānjiē)
voyage.content: Housed in the 1954-built Block C of the former Grand Hôtel de Pékin, built in a fusion of Stalinist and traditional Chinese architectural styles.

voyage.name: Grand Hyatt Beijing
voyage.alt: 北京东方君悦大酒店; Běijīng dōngfāng jūnyuè dàiǔdiàn
voyage.address: 1 East Chang'an Avenue (东长安街1号, Dōngcháng'ānjiē
voyage.content: Privately-owned, exquisite, and expensive 5-star hotel. There is an enormous swimming pool in the basement that is decorated in very tropical manner, but the deepest part is only 1.5 m (5 ft). The jacuzzi and wet sauna are excellent. Great hotel and great location, if you can afford it.

voyage.name: Legendale Hotel Beijing
voyage.alt: 北京励骏酒店; Běijīng Lìjùn Jiǔdiàn
voyage.price: Listed rates for doubles ¥4,140-7,820, discounted rates ¥1,478-5,797
voyage.address: 90-92 Jinbao Street (金宝街90-92号; Jīnbǎojiē)
voyage.content: Five-star hotel located close to Wangfujing. Rooms of 38-71 m² with free Internet. Business center, beauty salon, karaoke, fitness, swimming pool, massage and sauna available. Chinese and Western restaurants, coffee shop and bar.

voyage.name: Regent Beijing
voyage.alt: 北京丽晶酒店;Běijīng lì jīng jiǔdiàn
voyage.address: 99 Jinbao St, Dong Dan, Dongcheng, Beijing, China, 100005
voyage.content: Large luxury hotel with buffet breakfast, an indoor pool, a spa, and fitness center.

voyage.name: The Peninsula Beijing
voyage.alt: 北京王府半岛酒店; Běijīng Wángfǔbàndǎo Jiǔdiàn
voyage.price: Listed rates for doubles from ¥3,400, discounted from ¥1,500, breakfast ¥299
voyage.address: 8 Jinyu Hutong, Wangfujing (王府井金鱼胡同8号; Wángfǔjǐng Jīnyúhútòng)
voyage.content: Five-star hotel with rooms with free internet. The smallest rooms are 31 m². Swimming pool, spa, massage and lots of shops available. Chinese and Western restaurants as well as a bar.

voyage.name: Xinhai Jin Jiang Hotel
voyage.alt: 鑫海锦江大酒店; Xīnhǎi jǐnjiāng dàjiǔdiàn
voyage.address: 61 Jinbao Street (金宝街61号, Jīnbǎojiē)
voyage.content: In the bustling commercial district of Wangfujing, this hotel has 231 elegantly furnished rooms. It has excellent business and leisure facilities which include the sprawling International Conference Center.
